Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

title: Add-on STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Validation

The prefix and suffix segments are static and never part of what gets validated - validation applies only to the core input value, and the add-on itself visually anchors the format that value is expected to match.

Required marking - mark the field as a whole required, next to its label, the same as any text field - the add-on segment doesn't change how required state is shown.
Format validation - check the typed value against the format the add-on implies, not a generic pattern - a username field with an "@company.com" suffix should validate the local-part on blur, since the add-on already fixes the rest of the format.
Error message - reference the add-on's format directly, e.g. "Enter a username before @company.com," rather than a generic "Invalid input" that leaves the user guessing what "before @company.com" even means.
Recovery - keep the add-on visible and unchanged while the core value is in an error state, so the expected format stays in view as the user corrects the input.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Add-on is a single-line text field with a fixed, non-editable prefix and/or suffix segment attached directly to it - used when the value alone would be ambiguous or would force the user to retype a constant part of it every time.

WHEN TO USE

A value with a fixed protocol or domain prefix - https:// before a URL.
A currency symbol on a price - $ before a numeric amount.
A username handle with a fixed platform prefix - @ before a handle, or a fixed email domain suffix.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A value with no natural constant part - use a plain Input - adding an empty or irrelevant add-on segment is just visual noise.
A prefix/suffix that the user should be able to edit or choose - use a Select alongside the field, or a Group Button, instead of a fixed, non-editable add-on.
Multiple independent constant parts on both sides that combine in complex ways - consider breaking the field into clearly labeled separate inputs instead.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the add-on segment visually distinct but clearly non-editable (different background, no cursor) so users don't try to click into it.
Use the add-on only for a genuinely constant part of the value - never for something that varies per use case.
Make sure the combined value (prefix + typed value + suffix) is what actually gets submitted, not just displayed.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Price
£
per month

The add-ons carry the unit, so the input holds only the number the user actually has to type.

DON'T

Price
Set the amount

An add-on used as a label steals the width the value needs and leaves the field itself unlabelled. Add-ons are for units and fixed fragments, not instructions.

ACCESSIBILITY

The prefix/suffix text is exposed to assistive technology alongside the field's label, so its meaning isn't lost for screen-reader users.
The editable portion remains a real, independently focusable input - the add-on segments are not part of the tab order since they aren't interactive.
Sufficient contrast between the add-on segment and the editable field, so the boundary between fixed and editable text is visually clear.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Input, Select, Number.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Add-on component system for the Agentic Design System.

An Add-on is a single-line text field with an optional prefix segment and/or suffix segment attached directly to it, sharing one visual control - like a protocol prefix on a URL field or a currency/unit suffix on a price field. Each segment has its own subtle background, distinct from the input area, so it reads as a separate attached zone rather than plain field background.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focused: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style. Segments nest inside the control's own radius on their outer corner only.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show prefix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the left edge of the field with its own editable prefix text - e.g. a protocol or currency symbol), Show suffix (boolean, optional text segment attached to the right edge of the field with its own editable suffix text - e.g. a domain or unit).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Affix component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, offset, state, content) - a wrapper that pins its child element to the viewport once the page scrolls past the child's original position, so it stays reachable.

Types (2):
- Top: pins the element 8px from the top of the viewport once scrolled past.
- Bottom: pins the element 8px from the bottom of the viewport once scrolled past.

States (3):
- Rest: the element sits in its normal position in the page flow - not yet affixed.
- Affixed: the element is pinned to its edge, visually lifted with a shadow and a slightly stronger border/background so it reads as detached from the page flow beneath it.
- Disabled: affix behavior is turned off entirely - the element always stays in its normal flow position, shown dimmed here to distinguish it from Rest.

Component properties: Content label (text, e.g. "AuditField42" - the content being pinned, such as a toolbar or a call-to-action); Offset (number, px from the edge once affixed) - currently 8.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Affix component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, offset, state, content) - a wrapper that pins its child element to the viewport once the page scrolls past the child's original position, so it stays reachable.

Types (2):
- Top: pins the element 9px from the top of the viewport once scrolled past.
- Bottom: pins the element 9px from the bottom of the viewport once scrolled past.

States (3):
- Rest: the element sits in its normal position in the page flow - not yet affixed.
- Affixed: the element is pinned to its edge, visually lifted with a shadow and a slightly stronger border/background so it reads as detached from the page flow beneath it.
- Disabled: affix behavior is turned off entirely - the element always stays in its normal flow position, shown dimmed here to distinguish it from Rest.

Component properties: Content label (text, e.g. "Filter toolbar" - the content being pinned, such as a toolbar or a call-to-action); Offset (number, px from the edge once affixed) - currently 9.

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Affix component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, offset, state, content) - a wrapper that pins its child element to the viewport once the page scrolls past the child's original position, so it stays reachable.

Types (2):
- Top: pins the element 8px from the top of the viewport once scrolled past.
- Bottom: pins the element 8px from the bottom of the viewport once scrolled past.

States (3):
- Rest: the element sits in its normal position in the page flow - not yet affixed.
- Affixed: the element is pinned to its edge, visually lifted with a shadow and a slightly stronger border/background so it reads as detached from the page flow beneath it.
- Disabled: affix behavior is turned off entirely - the element always stays in its normal flow position, shown dimmed here to distinguish it from Rest.

Component properties: Content label (text, e.g. "Filter toolbar" - the content being pinned, such as a toolbar or a call-to-action); Offset (number, px from the edge once affixed) - currently 8.

- Rest: the element sits in its normal position in the page flow - not yet affixed.
- Affixed: the element is pinned to its edge, visually lifted with a shadow and a slightly stronger border/background so it reads as detached from the page flow beneath it.
- Disabled: affix behavior is turned off entirely - the element always stays in its normal flow position, shown dimmed here to distinguish it from Rest.

Component properties: Content label (text, e.g. "Filter toolbar" - the content being pinned, such as a toolbar or a call-to-action); Offset (number, px from the edge once affixed) - currently 8.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Affix pins an element to the viewport once the page scrolls past its original position, so it stays reachable - distinct from Float Button, which is always corner-anchored regardless of scroll, and distinct from Header/Modal overlays, which aren't tied to scroll position at all.

WHEN TO USE

A filter or toolbar above a long list or table - stays available without scrolling back up.
A table's header row - column labels stay visible while scrolling through many rows.
A persistent call-to-action or a section sub-navigation - anything that should remain reachable throughout a long page.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A single, always-corner-anchored action unrelated to scroll position - use Float Button instead.
Short pages with no meaningful scroll distance - affixing adds complexity with no real benefit if the whole page already fits in view.
Elements that must stay in a fixed spot regardless of any particular trigger point - use a real fixed-position layout element instead of Affix's scroll-triggered pinning.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the affixed element visually distinct once pinned (a subtle shadow or border) so users notice it detached from the page flow.
Affix only content that benefits from constant visibility - overusing it on multiple elements at once creates a cluttered, competing set of sticky bars.
Account for the affixed element's height when it overlaps content below it, so nothing gets permanently hidden underneath it.

DO AND DON'T

DO

STICKY
Save bar - pins once its normal position scrolls out of view

Pins a short, persistently-useful action bar, and only once the page has scrolled past where it would normally sit.

DON'T

STICKY
Full article text - pinned for the entire length of the page

Pinning a large block of content for the whole scroll permanently eats screen space the reader needs for the content moving underneath it.

ACCESSIBILITY

The affixed element keeps its place in the reading/tab order - affixing is a purely visual position change, not a DOM reordering.
Sufficient contrast and a visible boundary (shadow/border) once affixed, so it doesn't visually blend into whatever scrolls beneath it.
Never affix content that would then overlap and obscure keyboard focus elsewhere on the page.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Float Button, Anchor, Tabs.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Alert component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an inline banner/message block embedded in page content (not a floating overlay like Toast), used to surface a status message such as "Your changes have been saved." It sits flush in the page flow, full width of its container, with a colored icon, title, optional description, and optional dismiss/action controls.

Types (4):
- Info: A neutral informational message - status updates, tips, and other non-urgent notices.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #4f8fe6
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Success: Confirms a positive outcome - a save, a submit, or another action completing as expected.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #2fbf6e
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention before it becomes a problem.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #e6a53a
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Error: Reports a failure or invalid state that is blocking progress.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #ff031a
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.

States (4, structural - change what's rendered inside the banner, not just its color):
- Default: title and description, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "Undo") after the description.
- Title only: title text only - the description is omitted entirely, regardless of whether a description value is set.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole banner.

Component properties: Corner radius; Title (text, default "Update available"); Description (text, default "A new version is ready to install.", omitted for the Title-only state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a colored status icon matching the alert's type).
Current values - Title: "AuditField42", Description: "A new version is ready to install.", Show icon: yes.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Alert component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an inline banner/message block embedded in page content (not a floating overlay like Toast), used to surface a status message such as "Your changes have been saved." It sits flush in the page flow, full width of its container, with a colored icon, title, optional description, and optional dismiss/action controls.

Types (4):
- Info: A neutral informational message - status updates, tips, and other non-urgent notices.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #4f8fe6
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Success: Confirms a positive outcome - a save, a submit, or another action completing as expected.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #2fbf6e
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention before it becomes a problem.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #e6a53a
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Error: Reports a failure or invalid state that is blocking progress.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #ff031a
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.

States (4, structural - change what's rendered inside the banner, not just its color):
- Default: title and description, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "Undo") after the description.
- Title only: title text only - the description is omitted entirely, regardless of whether a description value is set.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole banner.

Component properties: Corner radius; Title (text, default "Update available"); Description (text, default "A new version is ready to install.", omitted for the Title-only state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a colored status icon matching the alert's type).
Current values - Title: "Update available", Description: "AuditField42", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Alert component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an inline banner/message block embedded in page content (not a floating overlay like Toast), used to surface a status message such as "Your changes have been saved." It sits flush in the page flow, full width of its container, with a colored icon, title, optional description, and optional dismiss/action controls.

Types (4):
- Info: A neutral informational message - status updates, tips, and other non-urgent notices.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #4f8fe6
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Success: Confirms a positive outcome - a save, a submit, or another action completing as expected.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #2fbf6e
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention before it becomes a problem.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #e6a53a
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.
- Error: Reports a failure or invalid state that is blocking progress.
  Accent color (icon, title text, left border): #ff031a
  Background: #f1f1ee - ONE consistent background across every type, never tinted per type. Left border: 3px solid the accent color. Only the icon, title and left border ever carry the semantic color.

States (4, structural - change what's rendered inside the banner, not just its color):
- Default: title and description, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "Undo") after the description.
- Title only: title text only - the description is omitted entirely, regardless of whether a description value is set.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole banner.

Component properties: Corner radius; Title (text, default "Update available"); Description (text, default "A new version is ready to install.", omitted for the Title-only state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a colored status icon matching the alert's type).
Current values - Title: "Update available", Description: "A new version is ready to install.", Show icon: no.
