## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Validation

Autocomplete's suggestions are fetched, not static, so its validation contract covers the dropdown's async states as well as whether a typed value has to match the list.

Required marking - mark a required Autocomplete field the same way as any other required field in this system (red asterisk after the label).
Loading state - while suggestions are being fetched, show a subtle spinner or skeleton row in the dropdown rather than a blank flash - a blank dropdown reads as "no matches" before the request has even finished.
No-results state - if nothing matches, show a specific message like "No matches for '[query]'" rather than silently showing nothing.
Match requirement - decide up front whether the field accepts free text not present in the list, or requires an exact match from it. If it requires a match, validate on blur with a message like "Choose an option from the list" or "'[typed value]' isn't a recognized option" - don't let an unmatched value quietly pass through to submit.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Autocomplete is a text field that shows a live list of matching suggestions as the user types, while still accepting a free-form value the user keeps typing past the suggestions - a hybrid between Input's free text and Select's closed option list.

WHEN TO USE

A search-like field with known likely values - a city search, a product lookup.
Picking from a large option set faster by typing - a tag picker, a contact search.
A command or query input - where suggestions speed up entry but a fully custom value is still valid.

WHEN NOT TO USE

The value must be one of a small, fixed set with no free text allowed - use Select instead so an invalid value can't be submitted.
There's no meaningful suggestion source - a plain Input is simpler when there's nothing useful to suggest.
Hierarchical, drill-down data - use Cascader or Tree Select rather than a flat suggestion list.

BEST PRACTICES

Debounce suggestion lookups so fast typing doesn't spam a search on every keystroke.
Highlight the matched portion of each suggestion so it's clear why it appeared.
Always allow submitting the typed value even if the user never selects a suggestion, unless the field truly requires a match.

DO AND DON'T

DO

City
Manchester
Manila
Mannheim

A short list of real matches narrowed by what has been typed, so choosing is faster than finishing the word.

DON'T

City
Aberdeen
Adelaide
Albuquerque

Suggestions that ignore the query are noise the user has to read past. If nothing matches, say so instead of listing the top of the list.

ACCESSIBILITY

Implemented with combobox semantics, so the suggestion list is announced and arrow keys move through it without leaving the input.
The number of available suggestions is announced as they update, so screen-reader users know the list changed.
Selecting a suggestion with Enter or click produces the same result, and Escape closes the list without clearing typed text.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Select, Mention, Input, Cascader.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Autocomplete component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a text input that shows a dropdown suggestion panel of matching options below it while the user types or when focused, letting them either pick a suggestion or keep typing a free-form value - distinct from Select (a closed-option picker, no typing) and from a plain Input (no suggestion panel).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default autocomplete field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focus: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no suggestion panel visible yet.
- Open: the suggestion panel is visible directly below the field while the user is actively typing - panel content is 3 example option rows, with one visually highlighted as if hovered or keyboard-focused so the user can see which option Enter/click would select.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value with the suggestion panel closed - the user already picked a value or dismissed the panel.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Avatar component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, shape, presence state) - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier for a person, not a one-off image tag.

Content types (3):
- Initials: A colored circle showing the person's 1-2 letter initials - used whenever no photo is available.
- Icon: A colored circle containing a generic person-silhouette icon - a neutral placeholder for an unknown or anonymous person.
- Image: A circle filled with a gradient standing in for an illustrated photo placeholder - real image URLs are never fetched, so this represents where a person's photo would render.

Presence states (4, a small status dot in the bottom-right corner):
- Default: no status dot shown.
- Online: a small green dot.
- Away: a small amber dot.
- Offline: a small gray/dim dot.
These are structural/presentational variants, not interaction states - Avatar itself is not interactive.

Component properties: Size (24px / 32px - default / 40px / 48px, currently 24px - Small - font-size and the status dot scale proportionally with the box size); Shape (Circle / Square, currently Circle); Initials text (Initials type only, currently "JD"). Avatar.Group (a separate composition, not a per-avatar property): a list of Avatars overlapped with negative margin and a border matching the page background, with a Max count past which the final tile becomes a "+N" overflow indicator styled like a real avatar. Show as (Avatars / Names only) - whether the group renders as that overlapping avatar-circle stack, or as a plain vertical list of full names with no avatar graphic at all, for contexts where showing the avatar image isn't worth the space; both modes represent the identical list, including the same "+N" overflow count.

Create a complete Avatar component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, shape, presence state) - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier for a person, not a one-off image tag.

Content types (3):
- Initials: A colored circle showing the person's 1-2 letter initials - used whenever no photo is available.
- Icon: A colored circle containing a generic person-silhouette icon - a neutral placeholder for an unknown or anonymous person.
- Image: A circle filled with a gradient standing in for an illustrated photo placeholder - real image URLs are never fetched, so this represents where a person's photo would render.

Presence states (4, a small status dot in the bottom-right corner):
- Default: no status dot shown.
- Online: a small green dot.
- Away: a small amber dot.
- Offline: a small gray/dim dot.
These are structural/presentational variants, not interaction states - Avatar itself is not interactive.

Component properties: Size (24px / 32px - default / 40px / 48px, currently 40px - Large - font-size and the status dot scale proportionally with the box size); Shape (Circle / Square, currently Circle); Initials text (Initials type only, currently "JD"). Avatar.Group (a separate composition, not a per-avatar property): a list of Avatars overlapped with negative margin and a border matching the page background, with a Max count past which the final tile becomes a "+N" overflow indicator styled like a real avatar. Show as (Avatars / Names only) - whether the group renders as that overlapping avatar-circle stack, or as a plain vertical list of full names with no avatar graphic at all, for contexts where showing the avatar image isn't worth the space; both modes represent the identical list, including the same "+N" overflow count.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

- version: 1

Create a complete Avatar component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, shape, presence state) - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier for a person, not a one-off image tag.

Content types (3):
- Initials: A colored circle showing the person's 1-2 letter initials - used whenever no photo is available.
- Icon: A colored circle containing a generic person-silhouette icon - a neutral placeholder for an unknown or anonymous person.
- Image: A circle filled with a gradient standing in for an illustrated photo placeholder - real image URLs are never fetched, so this represents where a person's photo would render.

Presence states (4, a small status dot in the bottom-right corner):
- Default: no status dot shown.
- Online: a small green dot.
- Away: a small amber dot.
- Offline: a small gray/dim dot.
These are structural/presentational variants, not interaction states - Avatar itself is not interactive.

Component properties: Size (24px / 32px - default / 40px / 48px, currently 32px - Default - font-size and the status dot scale proportionally with the box size); Shape (Circle / Square, currently Circle); Initials text (Initials type only, currently "AuditField42"). Avatar.Group (a separate composition, not a per-avatar property): a list of Avatars overlapped with negative margin and a border matching the page background, with a Max count past which the final tile becomes a "+N" overflow indicator styled like a real avatar. Show as (Avatars / Names only) - whether the group renders as that overlapping avatar-circle stack, or as a plain vertical list of full names with no avatar graphic at all, for contexts where showing the avatar image isn't worth the space; both modes represent the identical list, including the same "+N" overflow count.

title: Avatar STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Avatar component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, shape, presence state) - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier for a person, not a one-off image tag.

Content types (3):
- Initials: A colored circle showing the person's 1-2 letter initials - used whenever no photo is available.
- Icon: A colored circle containing a generic person-silhouette icon - a neutral placeholder for an unknown or anonymous person.
- Image: A circle filled with a gradient standing in for an illustrated photo placeholder - real image URLs are never fetched, so this represents where a person's photo would render.

Presence states (4, a small status dot in the bottom-right corner):
- Default: no status dot shown.
- Online: a small green dot.
- Away: a small amber dot.
- Offline: a small gray/dim dot.
These are structural/presentational variants, not interaction states - Avatar itself is not interactive.

Component properties: Size (24px / 32px - default / 40px / 48px, currently 32px - Default - font-size and the status dot scale proportionally with the box size); Shape (Circle / Square, currently Circle); Initials text (Initials type only, currently "JD"). Avatar.Group (a separate composition, not a per-avatar property): a list of Avatars overlapped with negative margin and a border matching the page background, with a Max count past which the final tile becomes a "+N" overflow indicator styled like a real avatar. Show as (Avatars / Names only) - whether the group renders as that overlapping avatar-circle stack, or as a plain vertical list of full names with no avatar graphic at all, for contexts where showing the avatar image isn't worth the space; both modes represent the identical list, including the same "+N" overflow count.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

OVERVIEW

Avatar represents a person throughout the product - in a profile menu, a comment, a team list, or an assignee indicator - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier shown as an image, initials, or a generic icon placeholder.

WHEN TO USE

A user profile menu or comment author - identifying who's associated with an action or piece of content.
A team member list or an assignee indicator - showing who's involved at a glance.
A chat participant list - compact identification across many people at once.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Representing something that isn't a person or team - use Image or an icon instead - Avatar specifically implies identity.
A context where a full name is more useful than a small visual - pair Avatar with a name rather than relying on the image alone when precision matters.
A large, detailed profile photo display - use Image - Avatar is built for small, compact identification, not a full photo viewer.

BEST PRACTICES

Fall back to initials or a generic icon gracefully when no photo is available, rather than showing a broken image.
Keep sizing consistent within any one context (all comments the same avatar size, for example).
Use the presence/status dot sparingly and only when online/away/offline genuinely matters in that context.

DO AND DON'T

DO

JD

Two solid initials at a size that stays legible, with presence shown as a small status dot rather than competing text.

DON'T

JOHNATHAN

A full name crammed into a 40px circle is unreadable at any size. Avatars carry one or two initials - use a name label beside it for the rest.

ACCESSIBILITY

Carries an accessible name identifying the person ("Jordan Lee's avatar" or simply the person's name), not left unlabeled.
A presence dot's meaning (online/away/offline) is exposed in text or an accessible label, not communicated by color alone.
Initials fallback text meets sufficient contrast against its background circle.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Badge, Image, List.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Avatar component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, shape, presence state) - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier for a person, not a one-off image tag.

Content types (3):
- Initials: A colored circle showing the person's 1-2 letter initials - used whenever no photo is available.
- Icon: A colored circle containing a generic person-silhouette icon - a neutral placeholder for an unknown or anonymous person.
- Image: A circle filled with a gradient standing in for an illustrated photo placeholder - real image URLs are never fetched, so this represents where a person's photo would render.

Presence states (4, a small status dot in the bottom-right corner):
- Default: no status dot shown.
- Online: a small green dot.
- Away: a small amber dot.
- Offline: a small gray/dim dot.
These are structural/presentational variants, not interaction states - Avatar itself is not interactive.

Component properties: Size (24px / 32px - default / 40px / 48px, currently 32px - Default - font-size and the status dot scale proportionally with the box size); Shape (Circle / Square, currently Circle); Initials text (Initials type only, currently "JD"). Avatar.Group (a separate composition, not a per-avatar property): a list of Avatars overlapped with negative margin and a border matching the page background, with a Max count past which the final tile becomes a "+N" overflow indicator styled like a real avatar. Show as (Avatars / Names only) - whether the group renders as that overlapping avatar-circle stack, or as a plain vertical list of full names with no avatar graphic at all, for contexts where showing the avatar image isn't worth the space; both modes represent the identical list, including the same "+N" overflow count.

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "99+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "Active"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 6. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 99. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "Active".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "100+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "Active"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 5. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 100. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "Active".

Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "99+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "AuditField42"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 5. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 99. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "AuditField42".

Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "99+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "Active"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 5. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 99. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "Active".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "99+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "Active"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

Size: Default - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 5. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 99. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "Active".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

title: Badge STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "99+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "Active"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 5. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 99. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "Active".

Component Guide
Human View

OVERVIEW

Badge draws attention to a count, a new item, or a status without interrupting the flow - a small dot, number, or short status label typically overlaid on or placed beside another element, like a notification bell or an avatar.

WHEN TO USE

An unread notification count - a number badge on a bell or inbox icon.
A new-feature indicator dot - flagging something recently added.
An account status label or a cart item count - a compact signal attached to another element.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Standalone status text with no attached element - use Tag instead - Badge is meant to overlay or sit beside something else, not stand alone.
A count so large or so central to the task that it deserves its own visible number in the main content - don't shrink primary information into a small corner badge.
A persistent label describing a whole row or card's category - use Tag, which is built for that role.

BEST PRACTICES

Cap large counts with a "99+" style ceiling rather than letting the badge grow to fit an arbitrarily large number.
Reserve badge colors consistently (e.g. red for alerts, neutral for plain counts) across the product.
Remove or hide the badge entirely at zero/none, rather than showing an empty "0".

DO AND DON'T

DO

✉
3

A real count on the object it belongs to, so the number means exactly one thing: unread items in that inbox.

DON'T

Everything is fine, no action needed right now

A sentence-length label defeats what a badge is for - a glance, not a read. Keep the label to a word or two, or drop it for the dot alone.

ACCESSIBILITY

The count or status is exposed to assistive technology as text, not conveyed by a colored dot alone.
When overlaid on an icon button, the badge's information is included in that button's accessible name ("Notifications, 3 unread").
Sufficient contrast between the badge and whatever it's layered on top of.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Tag, Avatar, Notification.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Badge component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, color, size) - a small indicator, not a one-off number or dot hard-coded per screen.

Badge is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 3 forms, each in 4 semantic colors, each in 2 sizes.

Forms (3):
- Count: a small numeric pill overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element (an icon or button). Shows the current Count value, capping the display at "99+" once Count exceeds the configured Max count.
- Dot: a small plain dot overlaid on the top-right corner of a host element, with no number - just signals "there's something new".
- Status: an inline dot plus a text label (e.g. "Active"), used standalone rather than overlaid on anything.

Colors (5, apply to every form, matching Ant Design's own Status Badge set): Default (var(--red-500), this system's brand red), Success (var(--green-500)), Processing (var(--blue-500), pulses with an expanding-ring animation to signal something actively in progress), Warning (var(--amber-500)), Error (var(--danger-500)).

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small drops the Count pill to 16px/10px font and the Status dot+label to match - the host icon and every color stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Count (number, applies only to the Count type) - currently 5. Max count (number, applies only to the Count type, caps the displayed value at "N+" once Count exceeds it) - currently 99. Status label (string, applies only to the Status type) - currently "Active".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "AuditField42" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

Size: 32px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

Size: 44px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Breadcrumb component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a horizontal trail of navigational links showing the user's current location within a hierarchy, separated by a divider, with the LAST item always the current page (styled differently - not a clickable link, just text in a stronger color).

Types (2):
- Chevron: the divider between items is a small chevron-right icon.
- Slash: the divider between items is a literal "/" character.

States (4, apply to the FIRST link only - every earlier/later link besides it and the final current-page item stay at Rest):
  Rest: color:#69707D;
  Hover: color:#111827;text-decoration:underline;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.5;pointer-events:none; Use aria-disabled="true" on the link, not the native disabled attribute - links have no native disabled state.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Font-size scales proportionally, applied to the whole trail.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per breadcrumb item, current value "Home, Products, Shoes" - item count follows the number of labels entered). The last label is always rendered as the current page (a non-link span); every earlier label is a real link.
