## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "AuditField42", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

tests.from: Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.
tests.prompt:
Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "AuditField42", Show shadow: yes.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: no.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

Size: Default - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

Size: Default - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Card STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
- Hover: border-color:#69707D;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

When to use

Any time related content needs to be grouped into its own bordered container, distinct from the surrounding page.

Dashboard summary tile
Product listing

Settings section grouping
Blog post preview
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Card groups related content into a bordered container, with an optional cover/media area or a footer row of action buttons - a general-purpose content grouping used across dashboards, listings, and profiles wherever a distinct, self-contained unit of information needs visual containment.

WHEN TO USE

A dashboard summary tile - a self-contained block of related metrics or info.
A product listing item or a team member profile - grouping an image, title, and details together.
A settings section grouping or a blog post preview - any distinct, self-contained unit of content.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Content that's actually a single flat list of similar rows - use List instead - wrapping every row in its own Card adds unnecessary visual weight.
A small piece of contextual detail tied to a specific trigger - use Popover instead of a full Card.
Structured label/value data with no need for a border or media area - use Description.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep one Card focused on one coherent unit of content - avoid stuffing unrelated information into the same card.
Use the media/cover area only when a visual genuinely represents the card's subject, not as decoration.
Keep footer actions limited to the one or two most relevant actions for that card's content.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Q1 revenue report

Summary of bookings, churn and expansion for the first quarter.

One subject per card, with a title short enough to scan and body copy that fits without truncating.

DON'T

Q1 revenue report, churn analysis, and next quarter's hiring plan

Everything from this quarter and some notes on hiring too, plus a few other things worth mentioning here.

Stacking unrelated subjects into one card makes the title wrap past recognition and the card unclickable as a single unit - split it into two.

ACCESSIBILITY

When a whole card is clickable, it's implemented as a real link or button, not a div with only a visual hover style.
Heading structure inside a card follows the page's real hierarchy (an h2/h3, not just bold text) so screen-reader navigation stays meaningful.
Interactive elements inside a clickable card (like a footer button) remain independently reachable and don't get swallowed by the card's own click handler.

RELATED COMPONENTS

List, Collapse, Description.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Card component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a bordered container for grouping related content, in 3 forms and 4 states.

Types (3):
- Default: Title and body text only - the simplest form, for compact grouped content.
- With media: Adds a cover/media area above the title and body - useful for content with a visual, like a product or article preview.
- With actions: Adds a footer row of two action buttons below the body - useful when the card itself needs a primary action, like "View details".

States (4, apply to the whole card, not per type):
- Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
- Hover: border-color:#7F8694;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); A lifted shadow, distinct from the resting Show-shadow drop-shadow.
- Selected: border-color:#FF031A;box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #FF031A; Reads as a persistent chosen-state border indicating this card is the chosen one in a set, not a keyboard focus ring.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; No interaction.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card; With media's cover area follows the card's top corners only.

What size do you want? (Default / Small) Small tightens body-wrap padding to 10px/12px and drops title to 13px, body to 12px - the corner radius, type and state set stay identical at either size.

Component properties: Corner radius; Size; Title (text, default "Team standup"); Body (text, default "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room."); Show shadow (boolean, default checked - adds a resting drop-shadow beneath the card, even before hover, distinct from and combinable with the Hover state's own lift shadow).
Current values - Title: "Team standup", Body: "Daily sync at 9:30 AM in the main conference room.", Show shadow: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Reference base: **1rem = 16px**. Both columns are equivalent alternatives, not two values to apply together. rem responds to the browser root font size; do not lock the root size to disable user scaling.

Use rem for scalable typography and spacing; retain px for hairline borders and viewport breakpoints where the component guidelines require it. Percentages, em, viewport units, line-height ratios, weights, opacity and timing are not converted. Code examples retain valid syntax.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 32px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).
