## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 44px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 48px - XL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 56px - XXL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.

- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a multi-column panel anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Focus: real keyboard focus on the field, no panel visible yet.
- Open: the multi-column panel is visible directly below the field - 3 columns side by side (Continent, Country, City), each with 3 example option rows. Each column's currently-selected option is highlighted, and a non-final column's selected option gets a trailing right-chevron to show it reveals the next column.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the full selected path joined by " / " with the panel closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty). Multiple selection (boolean - replaces each option's single active-row highlight with a real checkbox, letting more than one leaf be picked across different branches). Search (boolean - a real input inside the trigger itself, narrowing the first column to matches with the matched substring highlighted).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Validation

A required Cascader has two invalid states, not one: nothing picked at all, and a path started but never finished - a user who picked Country and State but never reached City has technically "touched" the field, so the error needs to say which level is still open rather than treating both cases the same.

Required marking - the red asterisk sits on the field label, same as Select, regardless of how many levels the path has.
Validation timing - validate on blur (closing the panel without reaching a leaf) and again on submit, so an incomplete path is caught the moment the user moves on, not only at the end of the form.
Error message - distinguish the two failure modes: "Choose a location" when nothing is selected at all, versus "Choose a city to finish this selection" when Country and State are picked but City isn't - a generic "Required field" doesn't tell the user which column to reopen.
Recovery - reopening the panel from an incomplete-path error should land on the column where the path stopped, not back at column one, so the user resumes rather than restarts.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Cascader selects hierarchical, multi-level data - like Country / State / City - through a multi-column panel where picking an option in one column reveals the next column's choices, letting the user drill down step by step to a final value.

WHEN TO USE

A hierarchical address or location field - Country, then State/Province, then City.
A category drill-down - a top-level category narrowing into subcategories.
An org chart or file-path picker - any strictly nested structure with a clear parent-to-child relationship.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A single flat list with no hierarchy - use Select instead - Cascader's multi-column panel adds unneeded complexity for a non-nested choice.
Data that's nested but the user needs to see the whole tree at once, expanding and collapsing branches freely - use Tree Select instead of Cascader's linked-column drill-down.
Free-form text with a suggestion list - use Autocomplete, not a fixed hierarchical structure.

BEST PRACTICES

Show the full selected path in the closed trigger (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai"), not just the final leaf value.
Keep each column's option count reasonable - if the deepest level has hundreds of items, add search/filtering within the column.
Let users jump back to an earlier column to change a prior choice without restarting the whole selection.

DO AND DON'T

ACCESSIBILITY

Each column is independently reachable and operable by keyboard, with arrow keys moving within a column and revealing the next one on selection.
The currently selected path at every level is announced as the user drills down, not only shown visually.
The trigger's accessible name reflects the full selected path once a choice is made.

Create a complete Cascader component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is a select-like trigger field showing a selected hierarchical path (e.g. "Asia / India / Mumbai") with a trailing chevron icon, that opens a MULTI-COLUMN panel below it (one column per level: Continent, then Country, then City) where picking an option in an earlier column determines what the next column shows, letting the user drill down to a final leaf value - distinct from Select (one flat list, no drill-down) and from Autocomplete (a single suggestion list, not multiple linked columns).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default cascader field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.

  Unchecked: background:transparent;border-color:rgba(15,15,10,0.15);

Create a complete Checkbox component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a small square selection control with 3 possible values (unchecked, checked, indeterminate), always paired with a text label, not a one-off checkbox glued to text.

Types (2):
- Standard: Just the box and its label, inline - the default treatment for a single agreement checkbox or a compact list of options.
  Unchecked: background:transparent;border-color:rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Checked: background:#FF031A;border-color:#FF031A; White checkmark icon (#FFFFFF).
  Indeterminate: background:#FF031A;border-color:#FF031A; White horizontal dash icon (#FFFFFF) instead of the checkmark.
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so the control stays visible against any background.
- Card: The box and label wrapped in a bordered row that highlights as a whole (background var(--red-tint), border var(--red-500)) when checked - useful for settings lists or selectable option cards where the entire row should read as selected, not just the box.
  Unchecked: background:transparent;border-color:rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Checked: background:#FF031A;border-color:#FF031A; White checkmark icon (#FFFFFF).
  Indeterminate: background:#FF031A;border-color:#FF031A; White horizontal dash icon (#FFFFFF) instead of the checkmark.
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so the control stays visible against any background.
  Card highlight (applies to the whole row, only when checked): background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);border-color:#FF031A;

States (6): Unchecked, Checked, Indeterminate, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Checked and Indeterminate share the same solid-fill treatment, distinguished only by icon (checkmark vs dash).
- Indeterminate is set via the element's `indeterminate` DOM property at runtime, not an HTML attribute.
- Disabled applies 40% opacity and a not-allowed cursor to the control.

Size: 16px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the box's width and height in px.

What corner radius do you want? (2px - Sharp / 4px - Balanced / 6px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the box itself.

Component properties: Label (editable text next to the box).
