Create a complete Collapse component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an accordion-style panel with a clickable header (with an optional chevron indicator) that reveals or hides a body of content beneath it when toggled, useful for progressively disclosing long or secondary content.

Types (2, grouping styles):
- Bordered: Each panel has its own full border and rounded corners, with visible gaps between stacked panels - reads as distinct, separate cards.
- Borderless: Panels share only thin top/bottom divider lines with no side borders or radius, reading as one continuous grouped list.

States (3):
- Collapsed: header only, chevron pointing down/closed, body hidden.
- Expanded: header plus visible body beneath it, chevron pointing up/open.
- Disabled: header at reduced opacity, non-interactive, chevron dimmed, body hidden as if collapsed.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type only - Borderless panels never carry a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales header/body padding and the header text one step - body text stays fixed at 13px regardless of size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Header text (text, default "What's included in the free plan?"); Body text (text, default "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", shown only in the Expanded state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a chevron indicator on the right side of the header).
Current values - Header: "What's included in the free plan?", Body: "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", Show icon: yes.

Create a complete Collapse component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an accordion-style panel with a clickable header (with an optional chevron indicator) that reveals or hides a body of content beneath it when toggled, useful for progressively disclosing long or secondary content.

Types (2, grouping styles):
- Bordered: Each panel has its own full border and rounded corners, with visible gaps between stacked panels - reads as distinct, separate cards.
- Borderless: Panels share only thin top/bottom divider lines with no side borders or radius, reading as one continuous grouped list.

States (3):
- Collapsed: header only, chevron pointing down/closed, body hidden.
- Expanded: header plus visible body beneath it, chevron pointing up/open.
- Disabled: header at reduced opacity, non-interactive, chevron dimmed, body hidden as if collapsed.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type only - Borderless panels never carry a radius.

Size: Large - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales header/body padding and the header text one step - body text stays fixed at 13px regardless of size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Header text (text, default "What's included in the free plan?"); Body text (text, default "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", shown only in the Expanded state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a chevron indicator on the right side of the header).

Create a complete Collapse component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an accordion-style panel with a clickable header (with an optional chevron indicator) that reveals or hides a body of content beneath it when toggled, useful for progressively disclosing long or secondary content.

Types (2, grouping styles):
- Bordered: Each panel has its own full border and rounded corners, with visible gaps between stacked panels - reads as distinct, separate cards.
- Borderless: Panels share only thin top/bottom divider lines with no side borders or radius, reading as one continuous grouped list.

States (3):
- Collapsed: header only, chevron pointing down/closed, body hidden.
- Expanded: header plus visible body beneath it, chevron pointing up/open.
- Disabled: header at reduced opacity, non-interactive, chevron dimmed, body hidden as if collapsed.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type only - Borderless panels never carry a radius.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales header/body padding and the header text one step - body text stays fixed at 13px regardless of size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Header text (text, default "What's included in the free plan?"); Body text (text, default "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", shown only in the Expanded state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a chevron indicator on the right side of the header).
Current values - Header: "What's included in the free plan?", Body: "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Collapse STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Collapse component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an accordion-style panel with a clickable header (with an optional chevron indicator) that reveals or hides a body of content beneath it when toggled, useful for progressively disclosing long or secondary content.

Types (2, grouping styles):
- Bordered: Each panel has its own full border and rounded corners, with visible gaps between stacked panels - reads as distinct, separate cards.
- Borderless: Panels share only thin top/bottom divider lines with no side borders or radius, reading as one continuous grouped list.

States (3):
- Collapsed: header only, chevron pointing down/closed, body hidden.
- Expanded: header plus visible body beneath it, chevron pointing up/open.
- Disabled: header at reduced opacity, non-interactive, chevron dimmed, body hidden as if collapsed.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type only - Borderless panels never carry a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales header/body padding and the header text one step - body text stays fixed at 13px regardless of size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Header text (text, default "What's included in the free plan?"); Body text (text, default "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", shown only in the Expanded state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a chevron indicator on the right side of the header).
Current values - Header: "What's included in the free plan?", Body: "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", Show icon: yes.

OVERVIEW

Collapse progressively discloses long or secondary content behind a clickable header - the content stays hidden until expanded, keeping the page compact while still making the detail available on demand.

WHEN TO USE

An FAQ list - each question collapsed until clicked.
Settings section grouping or filter panel sections - organizing a long settings page into expandable chunks.
An order details breakdown or terms and conditions section - long content that most users won't need expanded by default.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Content everyone needs to see immediately - hiding essential information behind a click adds friction; show it directly instead.
A single, always-visible section with no reason to hide it - a static Card or plain section is simpler when there's no benefit to collapsing.
Switching between different views of content rather than showing/hiding one section - use Tabs instead of Collapse.

BEST PRACTICES

Make the whole header row clickable, not just a small chevron icon, so the hit target is generous.
Default the most commonly needed section open when there's a clear default, rather than collapsing everything.
Animate the expand/collapse transition smoothly so content doesn't just snap in and out abruptly.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Shipping details
Delivered by courier, 2-4 business days.

A header naming exactly what is inside, so opening it is a deliberate choice rather than a guess.

DON'T

More info
Details

Two panels both titled something generic give the user no way to predict which one holds what they need - they have to open both.

ACCESSIBILITY

The header exposes aria-expanded, reflecting whether its panel is currently open.
The header is a real, keyboard-operable button, not a div with only a click handler.
The expanded panel is programmatically associated with its header via aria-controls, so the relationship is explicit.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Tabs, Card, Description.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Collapse component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - an accordion-style panel with a clickable header (with an optional chevron indicator) that reveals or hides a body of content beneath it when toggled, useful for progressively disclosing long or secondary content.

Types (2, grouping styles):
- Bordered: Each panel has its own full border and rounded corners, with visible gaps between stacked panels - reads as distinct, separate cards.
- Borderless: Panels share only thin top/bottom divider lines with no side borders or radius, reading as one continuous grouped list.

States (3):
- Collapsed: header only, chevron pointing down/closed, body hidden.
- Expanded: header plus visible body beneath it, chevron pointing up/open.
- Disabled: header at reduced opacity, non-interactive, chevron dimmed, body hidden as if collapsed.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type only - Borderless panels never carry a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales header/body padding and the header text one step - body text stays fixed at 13px regardless of size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Header text (text, default "What's included in the free plan?"); Body text (text, default "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", shown only in the Expanded state); Show icon (boolean, default checked - shows a chevron indicator on the right side of the header).
Current values - Header: "What's included in the free plan?", Body: "The free plan includes up to 3 projects, 1GB of storage, and community support.", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 32px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 44px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 48px - XL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

Size: 56px - XXL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.
