Create a complete Date Range component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a single field showing a start date and an end date separated by an arrow, with a fixed trailing calendar icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a calendar panel rather than typed character-by-character. It picks a start/end pair together instead of two separate date fields. Scope is the trigger field itself, in all its states - not an interactive calendar popup grid.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default date range field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected start and end date values (e.g. Jan 4, 2026 -> Jan 9, 2026) instead of the two placeholders.
- Error: shows an invalid/incomplete pairing (e.g. an end date before the start date) and pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Start placeholder (editable text shown for the start date when no range is chosen), End placeholder (editable text shown for the end date when no range is chosen).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Date Range component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a single field showing a start date and an end date separated by an arrow, with a fixed trailing calendar icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a calendar panel rather than typed character-by-character. It picks a start/end pair together instead of two separate date fields. Scope is the trigger field itself, in all its states - not an interactive calendar popup grid.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default date range field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected start and end date values (e.g. Jan 4, 2026 -> Jan 9, 2026) instead of the two placeholders.
- Error: shows an invalid/incomplete pairing (e.g. an end date before the start date) and pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Start placeholder (editable text shown for the start date when no range is chosen), End placeholder (editable text shown for the end date when no range is chosen).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Date Range component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a single field showing a start date and an end date separated by an arrow, with a fixed trailing calendar icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a calendar panel rather than typed character-by-character. It picks a start/end pair together instead of two separate date fields. Scope is the trigger field itself, in all its states - not an interactive calendar popup grid.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default date range field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected start and end date values (e.g. Jan 4, 2026 -> Jan 9, 2026) instead of the two placeholders.
- Error: shows an invalid/incomplete pairing (e.g. an end date before the start date) and pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Start placeholder (editable text shown for the start date when no range is chosen), End placeholder (editable text shown for the end date when no range is chosen).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Date Range STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Date Range component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a single field showing a start date and an end date separated by an arrow, with a fixed trailing calendar icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a calendar panel rather than typed character-by-character. It picks a start/end pair together instead of two separate date fields. Scope is the trigger field itself, in all its states - not an interactive calendar popup grid.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default date range field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected start and end date values (e.g. Jan 4, 2026 -> Jan 9, 2026) instead of the two placeholders.
- Error: shows an invalid/incomplete pairing (e.g. an end date before the start date) and pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Start placeholder (editable text shown for the start date when no range is chosen), End placeholder (editable text shown for the end date when no range is chosen).

Trip dates
Reporting period

Validation

Two connected dates mean two layers of validation - each end's own date has to be valid, and the pair has to be validated together for order.

Required marking - mark the field required when the range as a whole is mandatory; state on the label or nearby copy whether both ends or just the start are required, since "required" is ambiguous on a two-part field.
Validation timing - validate each end's own date validity on blur, but only check the start-before-end relationship once both ends have a value. Checking it right after the start is filled would incorrectly flag an incomplete range as an error.
Invalid date entry - a malformed or out-of-range date in either field is rejected with the same specific messaging as Date Picker (e.g. "February has only 28 days in 2026"), scoped to whichever end produced it.
Range order - if the end date lands before the start date, show "End date must be on or after the start date." Prevent most of these outright by disabling dates before the start in the end-date calendar once a start is chosen, or auto-adjusting the other end.
Error message - show the message inline, next to whichever segment (start or end) it applies to, so the user isn't left guessing which half of the range is wrong.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Date Range collects a start and end date together as one bounded pair in a single field - a text field showing both dates with a fixed trailing calendar icon - used whenever the two dates are meaningless apart, like a trip's start and end.

WHEN TO USE

Trip or booking dates - start and end, considered together.
A reporting period or subscription term - a bounded window with a clear start and end.
An event's duration - where showing just one date without the other would be incomplete.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Two genuinely independent dates - use two separate Date Pickers if the dates don't form one bounded range.
A single date with no end boundary - use Date Picker.
A numeric range rather than a date range - use Slider or two Number fields.

BEST PRACTICES

Show both dates together in the field so the pair reads as one value, not two.
Prevent selecting an end date before the start date directly in the calendar UI, rather than only validating after submission.
Highlight the in-between days in the calendar panel while the user is choosing the range, so the selection reads clearly before it's confirmed.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Two independent Date Pickers let the user build an impossible range and only find out when they submit.

ACCESSIBILITY

Announces which end of the range (start or end) is currently being selected as the user moves through the calendar.
Fully keyboard-operable, matching Date Picker's arrow-key and Enter/Escape behavior, extended across two linked selections.
The field's accessible name or nearby label clarifies that a range, not a single date, is being collected.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Date Picker, Calendar, Time.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Date Range component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a single field showing a start date and an end date separated by an arrow, with a fixed trailing calendar icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a calendar panel rather than typed character-by-character. It picks a start/end pair together instead of two separate date fields. Scope is the trigger field itself, in all its states - not an interactive calendar popup grid.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default date range field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focused: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected start and end date values (e.g. Jan 4, 2026 -> Jan 9, 2026) instead of the two placeholders.
- Error: shows an invalid/incomplete pairing (e.g. an end date before the start date) and pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Start placeholder (editable text shown for the start date when no range is chosen), End placeholder (editable text shown for the end date when no range is chosen).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

- version: 1

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

Size: Middle - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.

default.prompt:
Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

OVERVIEW

Description displays a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel - label/value pairs arranged in a configurable grid of columns, used for read-only structured details rather than an editable form.

WHEN TO USE

A user profile summary - showing a set of fixed attributes at a glance.
Order confirmation details or account settings overview - a read-only recap of structured data.
A product specification sheet or support ticket metadata - label/value pairs that don't need editing in place.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Data the user needs to edit directly - use the appropriate form fields (Input, Select, etc.) instead of read-only Description.
A single flat list of similar items rather than distinct labeled attributes - use List.
Tabular data with many rows sharing the same columns - use Table instead of repeating Description panels.

BEST PRACTICES

Choose a column count that keeps label/value pairs readable without excessive line wrapping.
Keep labels short and consistent in tone (all nouns, or all short phrases) across every field in the panel.
Group related fields visually, with an optional section title, when the panel covers more than one topic.

DO AND DON'T

DO

STATUS

DON'T

A paragraph forced into a label/value row breaks the grid's alignment for every other field. Long-form content belongs in a Card or a text block, not a Description grid.

ACCESSIBILITY

Implemented with real term/description semantics (or an equivalent structure) so the label-value relationship is explicit to assistive technology, not just visual proximity.
Long values wrap or truncate with a way to see the full value, rather than silently cutting text off with no indication.
Section titles are real headings, not styled text with no semantic weight.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Card, Table, List.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Description component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, column count, size, section title) - a read-only label/value grid for displaying a set of structured details at a glance, like a summary panel, not a one-off table hacked together per screen.

Description is not interactive - unlike most components in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each usable at a configurable column count and size, optionally with a section title above the grid.

Forms (2):
- Default: clean spacing between label/value pairs, no cell borders - a minimal look.
- Bordered: each label/value pair sits in its own bordered cell, forming a compact table-like grid with 1px dividers between cells.

Each pair is a label (small, uppercase, dimmed) stacked above its value (regular weight, high-contrast). Long values wrap gracefully within their cell instead of overflowing or breaking the grid layout.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales item padding and both label/value font one step - column count and grid gap are independent of size.

Component properties: Columns (1/2/3, default 2, drives grid-template-columns for how many label/value pairs sit per row); Size; Section title (optional string, shown as a heading above the grid, currently "Account details" - With title state only, other states ignore it).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "AuditField42"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "AuditField42". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Center. Size.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Left. Size.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Right. Size.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. - 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.

Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

Size: Large - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Center. Size.

Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Center. Size.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.

Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Center. Size.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Center. Size.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. - concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
