title: Divider STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Divider component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (form, line style, size, text label, text alignment) - a thin rule that visually separates content, not a one-off <hr> or border hack rebuilt per screen.

Divider is not interactive - unlike every other component in this system, it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is purely structural: 2 forms, each in 3 line styles and 3 sizes.

Forms (2):
- Horizontal: a plain full-width horizontal line with no text, used to separate stacked blocks of content.
- Horizontal with text: a horizontal line broken by a short text label (e.g. "OR"), positioned at the chosen Text alignment.

Line styles (3, apply to every form): Solid, Dashed, Dotted - set via border-style. Line color var(--line-strong), label text color var(--text-dim).

What size do you want? (Small / Medium / Large) Scales line thickness and label font-size together - Medium is the line-weight shown above.

Component properties: Text label (string, applies only to Horizontal with text) - currently "OR". Text alignment (Left/Center/Right, applies only to Horizontal with text, controls how much line sits on each side of the label) - currently Center. Size.

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

OVERVIEW

Divider visually separates sections of content with a horizontal rule, with an optional text label breaking the line - a lightweight, low-emphasis break between related but distinct groups of content.

WHEN TO USE

A section separator - marking a clear boundary between two content blocks.
A form group boundary or an "Or" split between two actions - e.g. "Sign in with email" / "Or" / "Continue with Google".
A separator between inline items - adjacent to a Breadcrumb, or between items in a row.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Spacing alone would already communicate the separation - don't add a visible line where whitespace is sufficient - overusing dividers adds visual clutter.
A boundary that also needs to be interactive or collapsible - use Collapse instead of a plain static Divider.
Separating truly unrelated content that shouldn't appear together at all - a Divider implies related-but-distinct groups; unrelated content belongs on separate pages or panels.

BEST PRACTICES

Use a labeled Divider (with text) only when the label adds real information ("Or"), not as decoration.
Keep its weight and color subtle - a Divider should recede, not compete with the content it separates.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Personal details

Billing details

Marks a real boundary between two distinct groups of fields, so the eye knows where one section ends.

DON'T

First name

Last name

Email

A divider between every single field turns a short form into a fence of lines, drowning out the one grouping boundary that would actually help.

ACCESSIBILITY

Purely decorative in most cases, so it's hidden from assistive technology rather than announced as content.
When it also carries a semantic heading-like label, that label is exposed as real text, not baked into a background image.
Never used as the sole way to convey a structural boundary that should really be a heading or landmark.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Card, Collapse, Description.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Small - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (280px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Large - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (480px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "AuditField42"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

tests.from: Update your name, photo, and contact details.
tests.prompt:
Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "AuditField42"); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: off.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Drawer STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

OVERVIEW

Drawer is a panel that slides in from a screen edge above a dimmed backdrop, for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout behind it - the page stays visible and contextually present at the edge, unlike Modal's fully centered takeover.

WHEN TO USE

An edit-in-place panel - editing a record's details without leaving the list behind it.
A filter or settings side panel - adjusting options while keeping the underlying content in view.
A detail preview or a multi-step form that needs more room than a dialog - still tied to the specific context it opened from.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A short, focused decision or confirmation - use Modal - Drawer's larger size is unnecessary weight for a quick yes/no.
Content meant to persist as part of the page's normal layout - use a permanent panel or sidebar rather than a Drawer that must be explicitly opened and closed.
A brief, non-blocking status update - use Toast or Notification instead of a full sliding panel.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the underlying page visible and dimmed, not hidden, so context isn't lost while the Drawer is open.
Choose a consistent edge (commonly the right) for a given type of task across the product.
Warn before closing a Drawer with unsaved changes, the same way you would for a Modal.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Filters

Status, owner and date range - applied to the list still visible behind.

A side task with enough substance to fill the panel, kept beside the list it acts on rather than covering it.

DON'T

Discard draft?
Cancel
Discard

A one-line confirmation leaves most of the panel empty and still blocks the page to slide in. Use Modal or Pop Confirm when there is only a question to ask.

ACCESSIBILITY

Traps keyboard focus within the panel while open, and restores it to the triggering element on close, matching Modal's behavior.
Exposed as role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an accessible name (its title via aria-labelledby), announced as it opens - like Modal, this is focus management and an interrupting dialog, not a passive aria-live announcement.
Escape and a visible close control are both always available, regardless of what task is in progress inside it.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Modal, Popover, Steps.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Drawer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable panel component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a panel that slides in from a screen edge (Left, Right, Top or Bottom) above a dimmed backdrop (scrim), with a title bar (optional close "x"), a body, and (usually) a footer with Cancel/Save buttons. Left/Right are full-height and their Size controls width; Top/Bottom are full-width and their Size controls height instead. It reuses the exact same header/body/footer/button visual language as this system's Modal component, just edge-anchored instead of centered - for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout.

Types (4):
- Right: Slides in from the right edge of the screen - the far more common real-world default for edit panels, filters and detail views.
- Left: Slides in from the left edge of the screen - same structure as Right, used when the trigger or surrounding navigation sits on the left.
- Top: Slides down from the top edge, full width - useful for a global filter bar or announcement that needs to span the whole screen rather than sit in a side column.
- Bottom: Slides up from the bottom edge, full width - the standard placement on narrow/mobile viewports, where a side panel would be too cramped to read.

States (3, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/Save buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - an informational panel, no footer action buttons.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - same concept as Modal's own No-close state.

Size: Medium - on Left/Right, controls the panel's width (380px) and it stays full-height; on Top/Bottom, it controls the panel's minimum height instead (a separate, smaller scale, since Top/Bottom's own header+body+footer content sets a real floor a width-sized value would undershoot) and the panel stays full-width. Other options: Small (280px) / Medium (380px) / Large (480px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)
Corner radius applies to all 4 corners of the panel.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Edit profile"); Body text (text, e.g. "Update your name, photo, and contact details."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

## Dimensions: px and rem

Reference base: **1rem = 16px**. Both columns are equivalent alternatives, not two values to apply together. rem responds to the browser root font size; do not lock the root size to disable user scaling.

Use rem for scalable typography and spacing; retain px for hairline borders and viewport breakpoints where the component guidelines require it. Percentages, em, viewport units, line-height ratios, weights, opacity and timing are not converted. Code examples retain valid syntax.

| Token | px | rem |
| --- | --- | --- |

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Dropdown component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off buttons for each variant. It is a trigger button that reveals a menu of actions or commands when clicked - a real <button> element, not a form field, with no associated <label>, just its own text and a fixed trailing chevron-down icon. It is distinct from a Select trigger (which picks a form value) and from the menu panel it opens (a separate component).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default dropdown trigger style - a bordered button that works well on any background and reads clearly among a group of other actions.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Open: border-color:#FF031A;background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08); This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis trigger with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the button sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Open: background:#ffffff; This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (5, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Open, Focused, Disabled.
- Open: the menu is currently visible; the trigger takes on a pressed appearance rather than a plain hover.
- Focused: a real :focus-visible outline for keyboard navigation, independent of Open.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, real disabled attribute, no hover/open/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text inside the button, current value "AuditField42").

Create a complete Dropdown component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off buttons for each variant. It is a trigger button that reveals a menu of actions or commands when clicked - a real <button> element, not a form field, with no associated <label>, just its own text and a fixed trailing chevron-down icon. It is distinct from a Select trigger (which picks a form value) and from the menu panel it opens (a separate component).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default dropdown trigger style - a bordered button that works well on any background and reads clearly among a group of other actions.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Open: border-color:#FF031A;background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08); This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis trigger with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the button sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Open: background:#ffffff; This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (5, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Open, Focused, Disabled.
- Open: the menu is currently visible; the trigger takes on a pressed appearance rather than a plain hover.
- Focused: a real :focus-visible outline for keyboard navigation, independent of Open.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, real disabled attribute, no hover/open/focus feedback.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text inside the button, current value "Options").

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off buttons for each variant. It is a trigger button that reveals a menu of actions or commands when clicked - a real <button> element, not a form field, with no associated <label>, just its own text and a fixed trailing chevron-down icon. Create a complete Dropdown component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off buttons for each variant. It is a trigger button that reveals a menu of actions or commands when clicked - a real <button> element, not a form field, with no associated <label>, just its own text and a fixed trailing chevron-down icon. It is distinct from a Select trigger (which picks a form value) and from the menu panel it opens (a separate component).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default dropdown trigger style - a bordered button that works well on any background and reads clearly among a group of other actions.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Open: border-color:#FF031A;background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08); This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis trigger with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the button sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Open: background:#ffffff; This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (5, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Open, Focused, Disabled.
- Open: the menu is currently visible; the trigger takes on a pressed appearance rather than a plain hover.
- Focused: a real :focus-visible outline for keyboard navigation, independent of Open.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, real disabled attribute, no hover/open/focus feedback.

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text inside the button, current value "Options").

Create a complete Dropdown component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off buttons for each variant. It is a trigger button that reveals a menu of actions or commands when clicked - a real <button> element, not a form field, with no associated <label>, just its own text and a fixed trailing chevron-down icon. It is distinct from a Select trigger (which picks a form value) and from the menu panel it opens (a separate component).

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default dropdown trigger style - a bordered button that works well on any background and reads clearly among a group of other actions.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Open: border-color:#FF031A;background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08); This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis trigger with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the button sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Open: background:#ffffff; This is the state while its menu is visible - the trigger stays visually pressed so the connection to the open menu reads clearly.
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Real keyboard focus, independent of Open - never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (5, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Open, Focused, Disabled.
- Open: the menu is currently visible; the trigger takes on a pressed appearance rather than a plain hover.
- Focused: a real :focus-visible outline for keyboard navigation, independent of Open.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, real disabled attribute, no hover/open/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text inside the button, current value "Options").
