Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 48px - XL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 56px - XXL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

- version: 1

- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Group Button STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Pressed: background:#e3e3df;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;color:#111827;
  Pressed: background:#c7c7c1;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

OVERVIEW

Group Button is a segmented control for switching between a small, fixed set of mutually exclusive options - one bordered strip of adjoining buttons where exactly one segment is active at a time, unlike Radio's separate circular inputs or Select's collapsed dropdown.

WHEN TO USE

A view toggle - switching between List and Grid layouts.
A time range or sort filter - Day/Week/Month, or a sort-order picker.
A short, fixed set of exclusive settings - unit system (Metric/Imperial), text alignment.

WHEN NOT TO USE

More than five or six options - segments get cramped; use Select or Dropdown instead.
Options that aren't mutually exclusive - use a Checkbox group so more than one can be active.
A single on/off setting - use Switch - Group Button is for choosing among several options, not toggling one.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep segment labels short (a word or an icon) so they never wrap or truncate.
Use it for exactly one active option at a time - it is not a multi-select control.
Keep the segment count small enough to fit without horizontal scrolling on narrow screens.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Day
Week
Month

A short, fixed set of mutually exclusive options, each label a single word, all visible at once.

DON'T

Last 24 hours
Previous calendar week

Sentence-length labels stretch the segments until the control no longer scans as a single row of choices. Use Select once labels get this long.

ACCESSIBILITY

Exposed as a group of real buttons with aria-pressed reflecting each segment's active state.
Visible focus ring per segment, independent of the active-state background fill.
The active segment is communicated by more than color alone (a filled background, not just a text-color change).

RELATED COMPONENTS

Tabs (switches views rather than options), Radio (separate visible inputs), Select (a collapsed single choice), Switch (a single on/off setting), Button (all 8 Button types - see Components · Button - for the standalone action that sits next to a Group Button rather than inside it).

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Group Button (segmented control) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of joined segments where exactly one is selected at a time, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Outlined: A bordered track with a divider between each segment - reads clearly on any background, no extra chrome besides the outline.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#D8DFEE;border-inline-end:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: background:#1c1f23;
  Pressed: background:#262a2f;
  Selected: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Filled: A solid track where the selected segment gets its own pill highlight - useful when the group needs to stand out as one cohesive control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#9CA6B4;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;color:#D8DFEE;
  Pressed: background:#383d44;
  Selected: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:-3px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (6, apply per segment): Rest, Hover, Pressed, Selected, Focused, Disabled.
- Only one segment is ever Selected at a time - selecting a new segment deselects the previous one.
- Disabled applies to the whole group at once (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not one segment at a time.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height, applied to every segment.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the group's outer corners only - the joining edges between segments stay square.

Component properties: Number of buttons (dropdown, 1-9, default 3 - drives both segment count and labels, one consistent lettered sequence: Option A, Option B, Option C, Option D, Option E, Option F, Option G, Option H, Option I); Field label (optional toggle, shows a label above the group, e.g. "View", mirrors the Input component's Label); Supporting text (optional toggle, shows helper text below the group, e.g. "Choose how to display your results.", mirrors Input's helper text).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Image component for the Agentic Design System. Build it as ONE reusable container for displaying a photo or graphic with graceful Loading, Error and Loaded states, in a configurable aspect ratio and corner radius, instead of a bare unstyled tag with no fallback handling. Types (2): - Default: the image frame alone, no caption. - With caption: the image frame plus a caption text row beneath it. States (4): - Loading: a pulsing shimmer skeleton block shown while the image is being fetched. - Error: a muted background with a small broken-image icon and "Failed to load" text, shown when the image fails to load. - Loaded: the photo fills the frame, with a small zoom icon overlay in the bottom-right corner hinting that the image can be clicked to preview. - Hover: the same as Loaded, but the zoom icon overlay becomes fully visible - in real usage this is a plain :hover rule on the frame, not a separate state class. What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the frame's corners. Component properties: Corner radius; Aspect ratio (Square / Landscape / Portrait, default Square - sizes the frame); Caption (text, default "Product photo", With caption type only). Current values - Aspect ratio: Square (160x160px), Caption: "https://example.com/audit-image.png" (With caption type only). Important: in real usage this wraps a real element, with onerror/onload handlers driving the Loading/Error/Loaded state classes above. Create a complete Image component for the Agentic Design System. Build it as ONE reusable container for displaying a photo or graphic with graceful Loading, Error and Loaded states, in a configurable aspect ratio and corner radius, instead of a bare unstyled tag with no fallback handling. Types (2): - Default: the image frame alone, no caption. - With caption: the image frame plus a caption text row beneath it. States (4): - Loading: a pulsing shimmer skeleton block shown while the image is being fetched. - Error: a muted background with a small broken-image icon and "Failed to load" text, shown when the image fails to load. - Loaded: the photo fills the frame, with a small zoom icon overlay in the bottom-right corner hinting that the image can be clicked to preview. - Hover: the same as Loaded, but the zoom icon overlay becomes fully visible - in real usage this is a plain :hover rule on the frame, not a separate state class. Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the frame's corners. Component properties: Corner radius; Aspect ratio (Square / Landscape / Portrait, default Square - sizes the frame); Caption (text, default "Product photo", With caption type only). Current values - Aspect ratio: Square (160x160px), Caption: "Product photo" (With caption type only). Important: in real usage this wraps a real element, with onerror/onload handlers driving the Loading/Error/Loaded state classes above. This is a static offline design system with no network access, so every cell shown here is a fixed CSS gradient standing in for "a loaded photo" - never an actual fetched image. ## Implementation contract Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. Create a complete Image component for the Agentic Design System. Build it as ONE reusable container for displaying a photo or graphic with graceful Loading, Error and Loaded states, in a configurable aspect ratio and corner radius, instead of a bare unstyled tag with no fallback handling. Types (2): - Default: the image frame alone, no caption. - With caption: the image frame plus a caption text row beneath it. States (4): - Loading: a pulsing shimmer skeleton block shown while the image is being fetched. - Error: a muted background with a small broken-image icon and "Failed to load" text, shown when the image fails to load. - Loaded: the photo fills the frame, with a small zoom icon overlay in the bottom-right corner hinting that the image can be clicked to preview. - Hover: the same as Loaded, but the zoom icon overlay becomes fully visible - in real usage this is a plain :hover rule on the frame, not a separate state class. Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the frame's corners. Component properties: Corner radius; Aspect ratio (Square / Landscape / Portrait, default Square - sizes the frame); Caption (text, default "Product photo", With caption type only). Current values - Aspect ratio: Square (160x160px), Caption: "Product photo" (With caption type only). Important: in real usage this wraps a real element, with onerror/onload handlers driving the Loading/Error/Loaded state classes above. Create a complete Image component for the Agentic Design System. Build it as ONE reusable container for displaying a photo or graphic with graceful Loading, Error and Loaded states, in a configurable aspect ratio and corner radius, instead of a bare unstyled tag with no fallback handling. Types (2): - Default: the image frame alone, no caption. - With caption: the image frame plus a caption text row beneath it. States (4): - Loading: a pulsing shimmer skeleton block shown while the image is being fetched. - Error: a muted background with a small broken-image icon and "Failed to load" text, shown when the image fails to load. - Loaded: the photo fills the frame, with a small zoom icon overlay in the bottom-right corner hinting that the image can be clicked to preview. - Hover: the same as Loaded, but the zoom icon overlay becomes fully visible - in real usage this is a plain :hover rule on the frame, not a separate state class. Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the frame's corners. Component properties: Corner radius; Aspect ratio (Square / Landscape / Portrait, default Square - sizes the frame); Caption (text, default "Product photo", With caption type only). Current values - Aspect ratio: Square (160x160px), Caption: "Product photo" (With caption type only). Important: in real usage this wraps a real element, with onerror/onload handlers driving the Loading/Error/Loaded state classes above. Create a complete Image component for the Agentic Design System. Build it as ONE reusable container for displaying a photo or graphic with graceful Loading, Error and Loaded states, in a configurable aspect ratio and corner radius, instead of a bare unstyled tag with no fallback handling. Types (2): - Default: the image frame alone, no caption. - With caption: the image frame plus a caption text row beneath it. States (4): - Loading: a pulsing shimmer skeleton block shown while the image is being fetched. - Error: a muted background with a small broken-image icon and "Failed to load" text, shown when the image fails to load. - Loaded: the photo fills the frame, with a small zoom icon overlay in the bottom-right corner hinting that the image can be clicked to preview. - Hover: the same as Loaded, but the zoom icon overlay becomes fully visible - in real usage this is a plain :hover rule on the frame, not a separate state class. Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the frame's corners. Component properties: Corner radius; Aspect ratio (Square / Landscape / Portrait, default Square - sizes the frame); Caption (text, default "Product photo", With caption type only). Current values - Aspect ratio: Square (160x160px), Caption: "Product photo" (With caption type only). Important: in real usage this wraps a real element, with onerror/onload handlers driving the Loading/Error/Loaded state classes above. This is a static offline design system with no network access, so every cell shown here is a fixed CSS gradient standing in for "a loaded photo" - never an actual fetched image. ## Implementation contract Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. Create a complete Image component for the Agentic Design System. Build it as ONE reusable container for displaying a photo or graphic with graceful Loading, Error and Loaded states, in a configurable aspect ratio and corner radius, instead of a bare unstyled tag with no fallback handling. Types (2): - Default: the image frame alone, no caption. - With caption: the image frame plus a caption text row beneath it. States (4): - Loading: a pulsing shimmer skeleton block shown while the image is being fetched. - Error: a muted background with a small broken-image icon and "Failed to load" text, shown when the image fails to load. - Loaded: the photo fills the frame, with a small zoom icon overlay in the bottom-right corner hinting that the image can be clicked to preview. - Hover: the same as Loaded, but the zoom icon overlay becomes fully visible - in real usage this is a plain :hover rule on the frame, not a separate state class. What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the frame's corners. Component properties: Corner radius; Aspect ratio (Square / Landscape / Portrait, default Square - sizes the frame); Caption (text, default "Product photo", With caption type only). Current values - Aspect ratio: Square (160x160px), Caption: "Product photo" (With caption type only). Important: in real usage this wraps a real element, with onerror/onload handlers driving the Loading/Error/Loaded state classes above. Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the frame's corners.
