Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Leading icon (boolean, optional icon before the input text), Trailing icon (boolean, optional icon after the input text - e.g. validation or a password-reveal toggle), Allow clear (boolean, shows an × button in the trailing slot once the field has a value, clearing it on click - takes over the trailing slot from Trailing icon whenever both are on and there's a value, since Ant never shows both at once).

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Leading icon (boolean, optional icon before the input text), Trailing icon (boolean, optional icon after the input text - e.g. validation or a password-reveal toggle), Allow clear (boolean, shows an × button in the trailing slot once the field has a value, clearing it on click - takes over the trailing slot from Trailing icon whenever both are on and there's a value, since Ant never shows both at once).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Leading icon (boolean, optional icon before the input text), Trailing icon (boolean, optional icon after the input text - e.g. validation or a password-reveal toggle), Allow clear (boolean, shows an × button in the trailing slot once the field has a value, clearing it on click - takes over the trailing slot from Trailing icon whenever both are on and there's a value, since Ant never shows both at once).

Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Leading icon (boolean, optional icon before the input text), Trailing icon (boolean, optional icon after the input text - e.g. validation or a password-reveal toggle), Allow clear (boolean, shows an × button in the trailing slot once the field has a value, clearing it on click - takes over the trailing slot from Trailing icon whenever both are on and there's a value, since Ant never shows both at once).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

title: Input Text Field STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Leading icon (boolean, optional icon before the input text), Trailing icon (boolean, optional icon after the input text - e.g. validation or a password-reveal toggle), Allow clear (boolean, shows an × button in the trailing slot once the field has a value, clearing it on click - takes over the trailing slot from Trailing icon whenever both are on and there's a value, since Ant never shows both at once).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Input (Text Field) is the base single-line text control for collecting free-form values - a label, a text box with a placeholder, and states for focus, filled, error and disabled - the foundation every more specialized text field (Password, Number, Search, and others) builds on.

WHEN TO USE

Any short, free-form line of text - email address, full name, company name.
A value with no fixed format the system can validate character-by-character - a search term typed into a form.
A phone number or similar short structured value with no dedicated component - when no more specific field type exists.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A value from a fixed, known list - use Select so the user picks rather than types a value that must match exactly.
Multiple lines of text - use Text Area.
A secret value that should stay hidden while typing - use Password.
A value with a live suggestion list - use Autocomplete or Mention.

BEST PRACTICES

Always pair the field with a visible label, not placeholder-only text - placeholders disappear once typing starts and fail low-vision and memory-impaired users.
Show validation errors inline, next to the field, with a specific message rather than a generic "Invalid input."
Use placeholder text only for a format example (e.g. "name@company.com"), never as the only instruction for what to enter.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Email address

A visible label that stays put, with the placeholder showing the expected format rather than carrying the meaning.

DON'T

A placeholder used as the label disappears the moment someone types, leaving the filled field unlabelled for anyone who looks away and back.

ACCESSIBILITY

The label is programmatically associated with the input (via for/id or by wrapping it), not just visually adjacent.
The error state sets aria-invalid and links the error message with aria-describedby, so screen readers announce it.
Focus state shows a visible outline distinct from the field's default border.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Password, Number, Search, Autocomplete, Mention, Text Area.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Input Text Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default text field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focused: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms or search-like inputs where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Leading icon (boolean, optional icon before the input text), Trailing icon (boolean, optional icon after the input text - e.g. validation or a password-reveal toggle), Allow clear (boolean, shows an × button in the trailing slot once the field has a value, clearing it on click - takes over the trailing slot from Trailing icon whenever both are on and there's a value, since Ant never shows both at once).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: no.

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Default - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Default - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Large - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

title: List STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete List component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show dividers) - a vertical stack of item rows for displaying a collection of similar items, each row with a title and description, an optional leading avatar, and an optional trailing action link.

Container styles (2):
- Default: No outer border - the rows stack directly against the page background, optionally divided by a thin line between each row.
- Bordered: The whole list sits inside one bordered, corner-radius'd container box.

Content states (4, apply to every row in the list at once):
- Default: Plain rows - a title and description only, no avatar or trailing content.
- With avatars: The same rows, each now showing a small leading initials-avatar circle.
- With avatars + action: The same rows with avatars, plus a small trailing text-style action link (e.g. "View") on the right of each row.
- Loading: The same row count and shape, but every value replaced with a Skeleton placeholder - so the layout doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Default / Large) Scales row padding and the leading avatar's diameter together (reusing Avatar's own h24/h32/h40 scale) - never font-size alone.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show dividers (boolean, default checked - shows a thin line between each row).
Current values - Show dividers: yes.

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

OVERVIEW

List displays a collection of similar items as stacked rows, like a notification feed, a team member roster, or a file browser - a straightforward vertical arrangement, simpler than Table's fixed columns and lighter than wrapping every item in its own Card.

WHEN TO USE

A notification feed or activity log - chronological or otherwise ordered similar entries.
A team member roster or file browser - a stack of comparable items, each following the same row layout.
A search results list - results that don't need Table's rigid column structure.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Data organized around several comparable columns per row - use Table, which is built for column-aligned structured data.
A small number of visually distinct, self-contained content blocks - use Card, or a grid of Cards, when items need their own visual containment.
A single set of label/value pairs describing one thing - use Description instead of a list of one.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep row layout consistent across every item, even when some items have more content than others (use consistent placeholders/spacing).
Show dividers or subtle spacing between rows so individual items stay scannable in a long list.
Pair with Pagination or infinite scroll once the list grows beyond a comfortably scrollable length.

DO AND DON'T

DO

DON'T

Update

Something changed in the system related to a record that was recently modified by a user in the workspace.

A vague title with a paragraph explaining nothing concrete forces the user to read every row in full to find out what actually happened.

ACCESSIBILITY

Implemented with real list semantics (ul/li or role="list"/"listitem"), so screen readers announce item count and position.
Interactive rows (clickable to open a detail view) are real links or buttons, not divs with only a click handler.
Any per-row action (like a remove or edit icon) has an accessible name identifying which item it applies to.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Table, Card, Empty.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Mention component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a multi-line free-form text field, styled like a compact comment box, that lets someone tag another person inline by typing "@" - a suggestion panel of matching people opens below the field, and picking one (or finishing typing a name) inserts it as an inline highlighted chip token mixed into the surrounding text. Distinct from Autocomplete, which replaces the whole field value with one chosen option - Mention inserts a token INSIDE a larger block of free-form text and can hold more than one mention in the same field.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default mention field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in a dense comment thread.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel of people anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the field sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
