title: Mention STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Mention component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a multi-line free-form text field, styled like a compact comment box, that lets someone tag another person inline by typing "@" - a suggestion panel of matching people opens below the field, and picking one (or finishing typing a name) inserts it as an inline highlighted chip token mixed into the surrounding text. Distinct from Autocomplete, which replaces the whole field value with one chosen option - Mention inserts a token INSIDE a larger block of free-form text and can hold more than one mention in the same field.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default mention field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in a dense comment thread.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel of people anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the field sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel of people anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus: field is empty, showing the placeholder - no chip yet, nothing typed.
- Open: the field looks focused and a suggestion panel is visible directly below it, listing 3 example people, each row showing a small round initials avatar and a full name, with one row visually highlighted as if hovered or keyboard-focused so the user can see which person Enter/click would insert.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing free-form text with one inline highlighted chip token mixed into it - the mention has already been inserted and the suggestion panel is closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally - Size controls the field's padding/font-size only, never its visible height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Validation

Mention adds async suggestion states on top of whatever validation the underlying text field needs - what shows while matches are being fetched, what shows when there are none, and whether an unresolved "@" fragment is allowed to stand.

Required marking - mark a required Mention field the same way as any other required field in this system (red asterisk after the label). When the form requires at least one valid mention specifically, say so in the field's helper text - "required" alone doesn't tell the user a mention is what's missing.
Loading state - while the suggestion popover is fetching matches for whatever follows "@", show a lightweight loading indicator inside it rather than leaving it empty. An empty flash between keystroke and results reads as lag or a broken query, not as "still searching."
No-results state - if nothing matches, show a specific, calm "No matches for '[query]'" message inside the popover instead of closing it silently. Closing without a message reads as a bug, not a deliberate empty state.
Unresolved mentions - when the field requires every mention to resolve to a real, selected entity rather than arbitrary trailing text, validate that on blur or submit with a message like "Remove or fix the unresolved mention '@[text]'," naming the exact fragment that didn't resolve.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Mention is a free-form text field that lets someone tag another person inline by typing "@" followed by a name, inserting a distinct chip in the middle of otherwise normal text - used for comments, chat, and any message field where notifying a specific person matters.

WHEN TO USE

Comments and team chat - tagging a teammate inline within a message.
Task assignment through free text - "assign to @Jordan" inside a longer note.
Code review and support ticket threads - notifying a specific reviewer or agent.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A field whose sole purpose is picking one person from a list - use Select or Autocomplete instead of a full free-text field with an embedded picker.
Plain free-form text with no need to tag anyone - use Input or Text Area - the "@" trigger adds complexity that's wasted if never used.
Tagging concepts, labels, or categories rather than people - use Tag or a multi-select Select instead of overloading the mention pattern.

BEST PRACTICES

Trigger the suggestion panel immediately on "@" and filter it live as the user keeps typing a name.
Render an inserted mention as a visually distinct chip, not plain text, so it's unambiguous who was tagged.
Let the user keep typing free-form text before and after a mention - it should never take over the whole field.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Comment
Ping @ali
AK
Ali Khan
AR
Alice Reed

Full name alongside the handle, so the right person is picked when two accounts start the same way.

DON'T

Comment
Ping @ali
@ali
@ali2

Handles alone give the user no way to tell the two apart, so the notification goes to the wrong person.

ACCESSIBILITY

The suggestion panel is reachable by keyboard (arrow keys to move, Enter to insert, Escape to dismiss) without ever requiring a mouse.
An inserted mention chip is announced as a distinct, named entity by screen readers, not read as raw "@username" text.
The field's placeholder or label makes the "@" trigger discoverable for first-time users.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Autocomplete, Text Area, Input, Tag.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Mention component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a multi-line free-form text field, styled like a compact comment box, that lets someone tag another person inline by typing "@" - a suggestion panel of matching people opens below the field, and picking one (or finishing typing a name) inserts it as an inline highlighted chip token mixed into the surrounding text. Distinct from Autocomplete, which replaces the whole field value with one chosen option - Mention inserts a token INSIDE a larger block of free-form text and can hold more than one mention in the same field.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default mention field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in a dense comment thread.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel of people anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when the field sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focus: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a suggestion panel of people anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus: field is empty, showing the placeholder - no chip yet, nothing typed.
- Open: the field looks focused and a suggestion panel is visible directly below it, listing 3 example people, each row showing a small round initials avatar and a full name, with one row visually highlighted as if hovered or keyboard-focused so the user can see which person Enter/click would insert.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing free-form text with one inline highlighted chip token mixed into it - the mention has already been inserted and the suggestion panel is closed.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally - Size controls the field's padding/font-size only, never its visible height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "AuditField42" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 28px - XS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 32px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 44px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 48px - XL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 56px - XXL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. - Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;

  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
