Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

Destructive item: if the last item's label is literally "Delete" or "Remove" (case-insensitive), automatically style that item's text and icon (color:#ff031a;) and add a thin top border (border-top:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.08)) on that item itself, separating it from the regular actions above - a common pattern real menus use to set a destructive action apart. Draw the border inside the item's own box (box-sizing:border-box) so it never adds extra spacing beyond the panel's normal item gap, and zero out that item's own top-left/top-right corner radius (border-start-start-radius / border-start-end-radius) so the line stays flush edge-to-edge instead of curling in with the item's own rounded corners - its bottom corners keep the inherited radius since it's the last item, sitting at the panel's actual bottom edge.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls each item's row height - padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the panel's outer corners only.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per item, current value "Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete" - item count follows the number of labels entered).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

OVERVIEW

Menu is the floating panel of commands or actions itself - what appears when a Dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. This component is the panel/list content, not the trigger that opens it, which is a separate concern handled by Dropdown or a custom trigger.

WHEN TO USE

The panel opened by a Dropdown trigger - the list of commands itself.
A right-click context menu - actions relevant to whatever was right-clicked.
A user account menu or bulk-actions panel - any floating list of clickable commands triggered from elsewhere.

WHEN NOT TO USE

The trigger button itself - that's Dropdown's responsibility - Menu is only the panel content.
A form value picker - use Select - Menu items are commands to run, not values to store.
Persistent, always-visible navigation - use a nav bar or sidebar rather than a menu that must be triggered open.

BEST PRACTICES

Group related items with dividers, and visually separate destructive actions (e.g. "Delete") at the bottom.
Keep item labels as short, specific verbs ("Duplicate", "Archive") so the whole menu scans quickly.
Close on selection, outside click, and Escape, consistent with Dropdown's expected behavior.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Rename
Duplicate
Delete

A top border separates the destructive action from the routine ones, so it cannot be clicked by momentum.

DON'T

Delete
Rename
Duplicate

Placing Delete first, right where the pointer lands on open, makes the riskiest action the easiest one to trigger by accident.

ACCESSIBILITY

Implemented with menu/menuitem roles, so arrow keys move between items and Home/End jump to the first/last item.
Disabled items are exposed as unavailable to assistive technology, not just visually dimmed.
Opening the menu moves focus into it, and closing it returns focus to whatever triggered it.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Dropdown (its trigger), Tag, Button.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Menu (floating panel of commands or actions) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, items) - the floating panel/list itself, like what appears when a dropdown trigger, a right-click, or a "..." button is activated. Not the trigger button that opens it, and not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Default: text-only items.
- With icons: each item gets a small leading icon before its label.

States (4, apply per item): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#D8DFEE;
  Hover: background:#1c1f23;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #FF031A;outline-offset:-2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Disabled: opacity:0.4;cursor:not-allowed;

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Small - controls the dialog's max-width (320px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Large - controls the dialog's max-width (560px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "AuditField42"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "AuditField42"); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: off.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Modal STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

OVERVIEW

Modal is a dialog box that appears above a dimmed backdrop to focus the user on one task or decision before returning them to the page - it blocks interaction with everything behind it until the user responds or explicitly closes it.

WHEN TO USE

A destructive-action confirmation - confirming a delete before it happens.
A short, focused task or form - terms acceptance, an onboarding step.
A media preview that needs full attention - viewing an image or document in detail.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A task that needs more room than a dialog comfortably allows - use Drawer, which slides in from an edge instead of interrupting the whole page.
A brief, non-blocking confirmation - use Toast or Alert - Modal's backdrop is a heavy interruption for something minor.
Frequent or repeated interruptions in a single flow - excessive modal use breaks flow; consider inline validation or a Drawer instead.

BEST PRACTICES

Give it a single clear purpose and a single primary action - avoid turning it into a small multi-purpose page.
Always provide an obvious way to close it (a visible close button and Escape), even when a primary action is required.
Keep destructive confirmations short and specific about the consequence, not a generic "Are you sure?"

DO AND DON'T

DO

Delete 3 files?

This cannot be undone.

Cancel
Delete

One decision, stated with its consequence, and a button that names the action rather than agreeing vaguely.

DON'T

Are you sure?

Please confirm.

No
Yes

"Are you sure?" with Yes/No never says what is about to happen, so the user confirms without knowing what they agreed to.

ACCESSIBILITY

Traps keyboard focus within the dialog while open, and restores it to the triggering element on close.
Exposed as role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an accessible name (its title via aria-labelledby), announced as soon as it opens - this is about focus management and interruption, not aria-live, since a Modal blocks and demands a response rather than passively announcing a status.
Escape always closes it, no matter the type or state. A visible close "x" is also available for Default and Destructive, unless explicitly hidden via the Show close property or the No-close state.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Drawer, Pop Confirm, Result.

Create a complete Notification component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state) - a corner-anchored card (solid background, border, left accent border, drop shadow, fixed ~260px width) with a semantic icon, a bold title, a longer description line and a close button, used to report a background or async event.

It differs from Toast by carrying more content per instance (icon + title + description + close, and optionally an action) for events the user wasn't necessarily watching for (e.g. "File uploaded successfully", "3 new messages received"), rather than Toast's brief, single-line, self-dismissing confirmation of an action the user just took.

Types (4, drive the left accent border and the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational background event - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Accent/icon color: #4f8fe6.

Create a complete Notification component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state) - a corner-anchored card (solid background, border, left accent border, drop shadow, fixed ~260px width) with a semantic icon, a bold title, a longer description line and a close button, used to report a background or async event.

It differs from Toast by carrying more content per instance (icon + title + description + close, and optionally an action) for events the user wasn't necessarily watching for (e.g. "File uploaded successfully", "3 new messages received"), rather than Toast's brief, single-line, self-dismissing confirmation of an action the user just took.

Types (4, drive the left accent border and the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational background event - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Accent/icon color: #4f8fe6.
- Success: Confirms a background or async task completed successfully. Accent/icon color: #2fbf6e.
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Accent/icon color: #e6a53a.
- Error: Reports that a background or async task failed. Accent/icon color: #ff031a.
Card (same for every type): background:#ffffff;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);border-inline-start:3px solid #4f8fe6;box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.35);

States (3, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: icon, title, description and a close (x) button - no action.
- With action: same as Default, plus an inline text-style action button ("Undo") below the description.
- Stacked: shows two of the same notification card layered with a small gap, the second one sitting slightly behind and reduced in opacity, to demonstrate multiple simultaneous notifications.

Component properties: Title (text, default "File uploaded"); Description (text, default "team-report.pdf is ready to share."); Placement (topRight/topLeft/bottomRight/bottomLeft, default topRight - which viewport corner the notification stacks in; multiple notifications in the same placement stack outward from the edge they anchor to).
Current values - Title: "File uploaded", Description: "team-report.pdf is ready to share.".
