Create a complete Number Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

The field is a single-line input restricted to numeric characters, with an optional trailing vertical stepper - two stacked buttons that increment or decrement the value by 1.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default number field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show stepper (boolean - shows or hides trailing increment/decrement buttons that adjust the value by 1), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the stepper that clears it).

Create a complete Number Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

The field is a single-line input restricted to numeric characters, with an optional trailing vertical stepper - two stacked buttons that increment or decrement the value by 1.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default number field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show stepper (boolean - shows or hides trailing increment/decrement buttons that adjust the value by 1), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the stepper that clears it).

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Number Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

The field is a single-line input restricted to numeric characters, with an optional trailing vertical stepper - two stacked buttons that increment or decrement the value by 1.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default number field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show stepper (boolean - shows or hides trailing increment/decrement buttons that adjust the value by 1), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the stepper that clears it).

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Number Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

The field is a single-line input restricted to numeric characters, with an optional trailing vertical stepper - two stacked buttons that increment or decrement the value by 1.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default number field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show stepper (boolean - shows or hides trailing increment/decrement buttons that adjust the value by 1), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the stepper that clears it).

title: Number STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Number Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

The field is a single-line input restricted to numeric characters, with an optional trailing vertical stepper - two stacked buttons that increment or decrement the value by 1.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default number field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show stepper (boolean - shows or hides trailing increment/decrement buttons that adjust the value by 1), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the stepper that clears it).

Validation

Number carries a format contract on top of the usual required-field rules - what counts as a valid character, when an out-of-range value gets flagged, and how the error names the actual constraint.

Required marking - mark a required Number field the same way as any other required field in this system (red asterisk after the label).
Validation timing - reject non-numeric characters at input time, so a letter or symbol never lands in the field to begin with. Min/max/step range checks are different: validate those on blur, not on every keystroke - flagging "5" as too low while the user is still about to type "50" is hostile and simply wrong.
Error message - name the actual constraint that failed: "Enter a value between 1 and 100" or "Must be a multiple of 5," never a generic "Invalid number."
Recovery - when the stepper is shown, clicking +/- from an out-of-range value snaps it to the nearest valid boundary, giving the user a one-click fix instead of forcing a full retype.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Number is a text field restricted to numeric input, optionally paired with stepper buttons to increment or decrement the value by a fixed amount - used anywhere the value is fundamentally a quantity rather than arbitrary text.

WHEN TO USE

A quantity someone adjusts up or down - cart quantity, guest count.
Any purely numeric value - age, price, a rating count.
A bounded value with a sensible min/max and step - where steppers make small adjustments faster than typing.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A number that's really an identifier, not a quantity - a phone number, a ZIP/postal code, a credit card number - use Input, since these are never incremented/decremented and often contain formatting characters.
A value that should be picked from a fixed list - use Select.
A range of two numbers - consider Slider for a bounded range with no need for exact keyboard entry.

BEST PRACTICES

Set sensible min/max/step values that match the real-world constraint (e.g. quantity can't go below 1).
Keep the stepper buttons a secondary input method - typing a value directly should always work too.
Show units alongside the field (e.g. "kg", "$") rather than expecting the number alone to communicate meaning.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Quantity
+
-

1 to 20 per order.

Steppers for a small count the user nudges, with the permitted range stated up front.

DON'T

Salary
+
-

Steppers on a value in the tens of thousands are useless - nobody clicks up from zero. Drop them when the step is not a unit the user thinks in.

ACCESSIBILITY

Uses the native numeric input semantics so mobile keyboards default to a numeric layout automatically.
Stepper buttons are separately focusable and labeled ("Increase quantity" / "Decrease quantity"), not just plus/minus icons.
Min/max boundaries are announced or otherwise communicated, not just silently enforced.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Input, Slider, Rating.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Number Field component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

The field is a single-line input restricted to numeric characters, with an optional trailing vertical stepper - two stacked buttons that increment or decrement the value by 1.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default number field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focused: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show stepper (boolean - shows or hides trailing increment/decrement buttons that adjust the value by 1), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the stepper that clears it).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

- version: 1

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 28px - XS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 32px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

- version: 1

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 56px - XXL - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

### Ownership and compatibility

- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

title: Pagination STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Pagination component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a row of page-navigation controls with one page always shown as current, not separate one-off buttons glued together.

Types (2):
- Numbered: Prev arrow, a row of page-number buttons and a Next arrow - lets the user jump straight to a nearby page, not just step through one at a time.
- Simple: Just a Prev arrow, a "Page X of Y" text label and a Next arrow - a compact control for when individual page numbers aren't needed.

Shared visual treatment (Numbered page-number buttons and the Simple type's Prev arrow):
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#111827;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;
  Current page: background:#FF031A;color:#FFFFFF;border-color:#FF031A;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  "Page X of Y" count text (Simple type): color:#4B5563;

States (4, apply per button): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- For the Numbered type, the current page (always the middle of the 5 numbered buttons in this reference) stays a solid filled state regardless of row/state being demonstrated on other buttons.
- For the Simple type, there are no individual page-number buttons, so states apply to the Prev arrow button instead.
- Disabled means the target button is a real disabled control (40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not just a visual style.

Use a left-chevron arrow icon for Prev and the same icon mirrored horizontally for Next (both real <svg>, stroke-based, 24x24 viewBox, currentColor).

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Controls the height of every arrow/page button; padding and font-size scale proportionally.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to each individual arrow/page button.

Component properties: Size, Corner radius. Page numbers/count shown are illustrative reference content, not a configurable property.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.
