Create a complete Password component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a single-line masked text input - dots hide the entered value by default, the same way a browser's native type="password" input renders. An optional trailing eye-icon button toggles the field between masked and plain text.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default password field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms like an inline PIN entry where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value (rendered as dots) instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a single-line masked text input - dots hide the entered value by default, the same way a browser's native type="password" input renders. An optional trailing eye-icon button toggles the field between masked and plain text.

- Outlined: The default password field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.

Create a complete Password component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a single-line masked text input - dots hide the entered value by default, the same way a browser's native type="password" input renders. An optional trailing eye-icon button toggles the field between masked and plain text.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default password field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms like an inline PIN entry where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value (rendered as dots) instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show reveal toggle (boolean - shows/hides a trailing eye-icon toggle button that switches the field between masked and plain text), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the reveal toggle that clears it).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Password STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Password component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a single-line masked text input - dots hide the entered value by default, the same way a browser's native type="password" input renders. An optional trailing eye-icon button toggles the field between masked and plain text.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default password field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms like an inline PIN entry where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value (rendered as dots) instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show reveal toggle (boolean - shows/hides a trailing eye-icon toggle button that switches the field between masked and plain text), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the reveal toggle that clears it).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

When to use

Any form field that collects a secret value the user is typing, where the characters should stay hidden by default.

Login
Sign up
PIN code

Validation

Password carries the same validation contract as any required field, plus rules specific to secrets - what counts as a valid value, when to check it, and how to keep autofill and password managers working rather than fighting them.

Required marking - mark a required password field the same way as any other required field in this system (red asterisk after the label) - this is separate from and in addition to the reveal toggle, which is about visibility, not requiredness.
Validation timing - never flag length or format errors while the user is still typing; validating on every keystroke reads as hostile and punishes someone mid-password. Check on blur or on submit instead. A live, non-error checklist of requirements met so far (green checks, not red errors) is fine and encouraged if space allows - it affirms progress without accusing the user of a mistake they haven't finished making.
Autofill and paste - set the correct autocomplete value (current-password on login, new-password on signup or change-password) so browser and OS autofill and password managers can fill the field correctly. A value placed by autofill or paste must be validated exactly like one typed by hand - never skip or weaken validation just because the value didn't arrive via keystrokes. Per WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication - Minimum), the field or flow must never require solving a cognitive-function test - transcribing a puzzle, remembering something from elsewhere, doing mental math - as the only way to authenticate, so pasting the password or accepting a password-manager fill must always work; never attach paste-blocking oncopy/onpaste handlers to this field.
Error message - state the rule directly and specifically: "Password must be at least 12 characters," not "Invalid password" or "Oops! Something went wrong." The user should be able to fix the value from the message alone, without guessing at what "invalid" means.
Recovery - the show/hide reveal toggle is the primary recovery aid for a failed validation: let the user reveal what they actually typed and compare it against the error message, rather than clearing the field and forcing them to retype blind.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Password is a text field that masks its characters by default, with a toggle to reveal the value temporarily - used for any secret the user is actively typing, so it stays hidden from anyone glancing at the screen while still letting the user verify what they typed.

WHEN TO USE

Login and sign-up forms - collecting an account password.
A PIN code or short secret - still worth masking even if numeric.
Changing a password or entering an API key - any value that shouldn't be visible by default.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A value that isn't actually secret - use Input - masking non-sensitive data only adds friction.
A one-time code delivered separately and meant to be read back to someone - consider whether masking helps or just adds a step; a plain Input or Number field may serve better.
Multi-line secret content - Password is single-line only; there's no dedicated masked textarea in this system.

BEST PRACTICES

Always provide the show/hide toggle - masking with no way to verify what was typed increases error rates and failed submissions.
Never restrict paste into a password field; blocking paste actively discourages the use of password managers.
Show password strength or requirement feedback near the field, not only after a failed submit.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Password

At least 12 characters.

States the rule before the user types, and lets them reveal what they entered so a typo is fixable rather than guessable.

DON'T

Password

Password does not meet requirements.

Hiding the rule until after submission, with no way to see what was typed, makes the user retry blind against a standard they still have not been told.

ACCESSIBILITY

The show/hide toggle has an accessible name that reflects its current state ("Show password" / "Hide password"), not just an icon.
Toggling visibility keeps keyboard focus on the field, so the user isn't forced to re-locate it.
The input still exposes autocomplete hints (current-password / new-password) so password managers can assist correctly.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Input, Number (for PIN-style numeric-only secrets), Text Area.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Password component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a single-line masked text input - dots hide the entered value by default, the same way a browser's native type="password" input renders. An optional trailing eye-icon button toggles the field between masked and plain text.

Types (3):
- Outlined: The default password field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focused: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Underlined: A minimal field with only a bottom border, useful for compact inline forms like an inline PIN entry where a full box would feel heavy.
  Rest: border-bottom:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-bottom-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-bottom-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-bottom-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing an entered value (rendered as dots) instead of the placeholder.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to Outlined and Filled - Underlined stays square, matching its minimal style.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when empty), Show reveal toggle (boolean - shows/hides a trailing eye-icon toggle button that switches the field between masked and plain text), Allow clear (boolean - once the field has a value, shows an × button before the reveal toggle that clears it).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Pop Confirm component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, state, question, confirm label, cancel label) - a small inline confirmation popover anchored to a trigger element, showing a short question with Confirm/Cancel buttons directly inside it, for lightweight "are you sure?" moments that don't warrant a full Modal.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

States (3): Default (a neutral confirm button, e.g. "AuditField42" with "No"/"Yes" buttons); Destructive (same layout, but the confirm button is styled in the danger/red color, for an irreversible or delete-type action); With icon (same as Default, but adds a small warning-triangle icon inline before the question text).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, matching this system's other floating-panel language (Menu, Autocomplete, Popover), but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The trigger sits on the ordinary page background outside the bubble, so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 1.5px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 6px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm). The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the bubble's own inverted background color. The Confirm/Cancel buttons sit in a right-aligned row below the question - Cancel is a transparent/bordered button using the bubble's own inverted text color (var(--text-hi) would go near-invisible against it), Confirm is a solid neutral button by default or a solid red button in the Destructive state, both with their own fully opaque background so they stay legible regardless of the bubble's inversion.

Component properties: Question (string, the short question shown in the bubble) - currently "AuditField42". Confirm label (string, the text on the confirm button) - currently "Yes". Cancel label (string, the text on the cancel button) - currently "No".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pop Confirm component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, state, question, confirm label, cancel label) - a small inline confirmation popover anchored to a trigger element, showing a short question with Confirm/Cancel buttons directly inside it, for lightweight "are you sure?" moments that don't warrant a full Modal.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

States (3): Default (a neutral confirm button, e.g. "Delete this item?" with "No"/"AuditField42" buttons); Destructive (same layout, but the confirm button is styled in the danger/red color, for an irreversible or delete-type action); With icon (same as Default, but adds a small warning-triangle icon inline before the question text).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, matching this system's other floating-panel language (Menu, Autocomplete, Popover), but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The trigger sits on the ordinary page background outside the bubble, so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 1.5px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 6px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm). The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the bubble's own inverted background color. The Confirm/Cancel buttons sit in a right-aligned row below the question - Cancel is a transparent/bordered button using the bubble's own inverted text color (var(--text-hi) would go near-invisible against it), Confirm is a solid neutral button by default or a solid red button in the Destructive state, both with their own fully opaque background so they stay legible regardless of the bubble's inversion.

Component properties: Question (string, the short question shown in the bubble) - currently "Delete this item?". Confirm label (string, the text on the confirm button) - currently "AuditField42". Cancel label (string, the text on the cancel button) - currently "No".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Pop Confirm component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, state, question, confirm label, cancel label) - a small inline confirmation popover anchored to a trigger element, showing a short question with Confirm/Cancel buttons directly inside it, for lightweight "are you sure?" moments that don't warrant a full Modal.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

States (3): Default (a neutral confirm button, e.g. "Delete this item?" with "AuditField42"/"Yes" buttons); Destructive (same layout, but the confirm button is styled in the danger/red color, for an irreversible or delete-type action); With icon (same as Default, but adds a small warning-triangle icon inline before the question text).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, matching this system's other floating-panel language (Menu, Autocomplete, Popover), but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The trigger sits on the ordinary page background outside the bubble, so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 1.5px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 6px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm). The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the bubble's own inverted background color. The Confirm/Cancel buttons sit in a right-aligned row below the question - Cancel is a transparent/bordered button using the bubble's own inverted text color (var(--text-hi) would go near-invisible against it), Confirm is a solid neutral button by default or a solid red button in the Destructive state, both with their own fully opaque background so they stay legible regardless of the bubble's inversion.

Component properties: Question (string, the short question shown in the bubble) - currently "Delete this item?". Confirm label (string, the text on the confirm button) - currently "Yes". Cancel label (string, the text on the cancel button) - currently "AuditField42".

title: Pop Confirm STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Pop Confirm component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, state, question, confirm label, cancel label) - a small inline confirmation popover anchored to a trigger element, showing a short question with Confirm/Cancel buttons directly inside it, for lightweight "are you sure?" moments that don't warrant a full Modal.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

States (3): Default (a neutral confirm button, e.g. "Delete this item?" with "No"/"Yes" buttons); Destructive (same layout, but the confirm button is styled in the danger/red color, for an irreversible or delete-type action); With icon (same as Default, but adds a small warning-triangle icon inline before the question text).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, matching this system's other floating-panel language (Menu, Autocomplete, Popover), but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The trigger sits on the ordinary page background outside the bubble, so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 1.5px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 6px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm). The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the bubble's own inverted background color. The Confirm/Cancel buttons sit in a right-aligned row below the question - Cancel is a transparent/bordered button using the bubble's own inverted text color (var(--text-hi) would go near-invisible against it), Confirm is a solid neutral button by default or a solid red button in the Destructive state, both with their own fully opaque background so they stay legible regardless of the bubble's inversion.

Component properties: Question (string, the short question shown in the bubble) - currently "Delete this item?". Confirm label (string, the text on the confirm button) - currently "Yes". Cancel label (string, the text on the cancel button) - currently "No".

Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Pop Confirm asks a short "are you sure?" question right next to the trigger that caused it, with Confirm/Cancel buttons inline in the popover - a lightweight alternative to a full Modal for confirmations that don't need to fully block the page.

WHEN TO USE

A delete or remove confirmation on a single row or item - anchored right at the action that triggered it.
Discarding unsaved changes or leaving a page - a quick check before a potentially costly action.
A bulk action or an irreversible toggle confirmation - still simple enough not to need a full dialog.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A decision with real complexity or multiple fields - use Modal - Pop Confirm is for a single yes/no question, not a form.
An action with severe, hard-to-reverse consequences at scale - consider a full Modal with more explicit warning copy for genuinely high-stakes confirmations.
Something that isn't actually a confirmation - use Popover for general contextual content that isn't a yes/no decision.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the question and both button labels short and specific ("Delete this file?" / "Delete" / "Cancel").
Anchor it directly to the triggering control so the connection between action and confirmation is obvious.
Close it on an outside click or Escape without treating that as a confirmation either way.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Delete this file?

Cancel
Delete

A single yes-or-no question, anchored to the control that triggered it, with buttons that name the outcome.

DON'T

Delete this file? Also remove it from shared folders, revoke links, and notify collaborators?

No
OK

Several decisions bundled into one question cannot be answered with one button. Once it needs this much explaining, use a Modal.

ACCESSIBILITY

Pop Confirm exists to gate a destructive or otherwise irreversible action, so its popover content carries role="alertdialog" rather than a plain popover/tooltip role - that's what gets its appearance and question announced together as a single interruption, instead of relying on the user to notice it visually.
Focus moves into the alertdialog (typically onto the Cancel button, the safer default) when it opens, and returns to the exact triggering element when it closes, whether closed by Confirm, Cancel, Escape, or an outside click.
The Confirm and Cancel buttons are distinguishable by more than color, especially when Confirm is destructive-styled.
Escape closes it exactly like a Cancel, never like a silent Confirm.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Modal, Popover, Tooltip.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Pop Confirm component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, state, question, confirm label, cancel label) - a small inline confirmation popover anchored to a trigger element, showing a short question with Confirm/Cancel buttons directly inside it, for lightweight "are you sure?" moments that don't warrant a full Modal.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

States (3): Default (a neutral confirm button, e.g. "Delete this item?" with "No"/"Yes" buttons); Destructive (same layout, but the confirm button is styled in the danger/red color, for an irreversible or delete-type action); With icon (same as Default, but adds a small warning-triangle icon inline before the question text).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, matching this system's other floating-panel language (Menu, Autocomplete, Popover), but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The trigger sits on the ordinary page background outside the bubble, so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 1.5px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 6px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm). The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the bubble's own inverted background color. The Confirm/Cancel buttons sit in a right-aligned row below the question - Cancel is a transparent/bordered button using the bubble's own inverted text color (var(--text-hi) would go near-invisible against it), Confirm is a solid neutral button by default or a solid red button in the Destructive state, both with their own fully opaque background so they stay legible regardless of the bubble's inversion.

Component properties: Question (string, the short question shown in the bubble) - currently "Delete this item?". Confirm label (string, the text on the confirm button) - currently "Yes". Cancel label (string, the text on the cancel button) - currently "No".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Popover component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, content state, trigger label, title, body) - a rich floating content panel (title + optional body text + optional close button) anchored to a real clickable trigger button, opened on click (not hover, unlike this system's Tooltip component), not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Simple (a bold title line only); With body (the title plus a body paragraph below it, e.g. "Storage usage" / "8.2 GB of 15 GB used."); With close (title, body and a small "x" close button in the top-right corner of the bubble, for dismissing the popover without clicking outside it).

Visual treatment: the same inverted-overlay bubble as Tooltip/Tour/Pop Confirm - near-black in light theme, near-white in dark theme, via the fixed var(--overlay-invert-bg)/-text tokens (never the user-customizable var(--graphite-900)/var(--text-hi)), so it always contrasts with the page regardless of theme or any saved brand color. No border on the bubble - box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" (matching this system's other floating-panel language, Menu/Autocomplete) gives it enough separation from the page on its own; a border read as an unwanted outline against the inverted background. Reads as a proper elevated panel rather than Tooltip's flat single-line bubble, with border-radius var(--radius-md) and room for a title/body/close button. The trigger is a real clickable button (not a decorative circle like Tooltip's trigger), styled like a simple bordered button on the ordinary page background - background var(--graphite-800), border 1px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 8px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm) - since it sits outside the inverted bubble, not part of it. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)), same background as the bubble, with only half of it showing - the rest tucked behind the bubble's own opaque background as a clean triangular point (same technique as Tooltip's arrow).

Component properties: Trigger label (string, the text on the trigger button) - currently "AuditField42". Title (string, bold text at the top of the bubble) - currently "Storage usage". Body (string, used by the With body and With close states) - currently "8.2 GB of 15 GB used.".

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Simple (a bold title line only); With body (the title plus a body paragraph below it, e.g. "AuditField42" / "8.2 GB of 15 GB used."); With close (title, body and a small "x" close button in the top-right corner of the bubble, for dismissing the popover without clicking outside it).

Visual treatment: the same inverted-overlay bubble as Tooltip/Tour/Pop Confirm - near-black in light theme, near-white in dark theme, via the fixed var(--overlay-invert-bg)/-text tokens (never the user-customizable var(--graphite-900)/var(--text-hi)), so it always contrasts with the page regardless of theme or any saved brand color. No border on the bubble - box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" (matching this system's other floating-panel language, Menu/Autocomplete) gives it enough separation from the page on its own; a border read as an unwanted outline against the inverted background. Reads as a proper elevated panel rather than Tooltip's flat single-line bubble, with border-radius var(--radius-md) and room for a title/body/close button. The trigger is a real clickable button (not a decorative circle like Tooltip's trigger), styled like a simple bordered button on the ordinary page background - background var(--graphite-800), border 1px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 8px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm) - since it sits outside the inverted bubble, not part of it. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)), same background as the bubble, with only half of it showing - the rest tucked behind the bubble's own opaque background as a clean triangular point (same technique as Tooltip's arrow).

Component properties: Trigger label (string, the text on the trigger button) - currently "Details". Title (string, bold text at the top of the bubble) - currently "AuditField42". Body (string, used by the With body and With close states) - currently "8.2 GB of 15 GB used.".

title: Popover STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Popover component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, content state, trigger label, title, body) - a rich floating content panel (title + optional body text + optional close button) anchored to a real clickable trigger button, opened on click (not hover, unlike this system's Tooltip component), not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Simple (a bold title line only); With body (the title plus a body paragraph below it, e.g. "Storage usage" / "8.2 GB of 15 GB used."); With close (title, body and a small "x" close button in the top-right corner of the bubble, for dismissing the popover without clicking outside it).

Visual treatment: the same inverted-overlay bubble as Tooltip/Tour/Pop Confirm - near-black in light theme, near-white in dark theme, via the fixed var(--overlay-invert-bg)/-text tokens (never the user-customizable var(--graphite-900)/var(--text-hi)), so it always contrasts with the page regardless of theme or any saved brand color. No border on the bubble - box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" (matching this system's other floating-panel language, Menu/Autocomplete) gives it enough separation from the page on its own; a border read as an unwanted outline against the inverted background. Reads as a proper elevated panel rather than Tooltip's flat single-line bubble, with border-radius var(--radius-md) and room for a title/body/close button. The trigger is a real clickable button (not a decorative circle like Tooltip's trigger), styled like a simple bordered button on the ordinary page background - background var(--graphite-800), border 1px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 8px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm) - since it sits outside the inverted bubble, not part of it. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)), same background as the bubble, with only half of it showing - the rest tucked behind the bubble's own opaque background as a clean triangular point (same technique as Tooltip's arrow).

Component properties: Trigger label (string, the text on the trigger button) - currently "Details". Title (string, bold text at the top of the bubble) - currently "Storage usage". Body (string, used by the With body and With close states) - currently "8.2 GB of 15 GB used.".

OVERVIEW

Popover shows contextual details, a quick action, or a small settings panel next to a trigger element, opened by a click rather than a hover - richer and more persistent than Tooltip, since it stays open until the user dismisses it or clicks elsewhere.

WHEN TO USE

Contextual details revealed on click - more information than a hover-only Tooltip can comfortably hold.
An inline help panel or a quick-actions menu - a small floating panel anchored to its trigger.
A filter/settings mini-panel or a user-info preview - richer content that benefits from staying open while the user reads or interacts with it.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A short, single-line hint - use Tooltip - Popover is heavier than a brief label needs.
A yes/no confirmation with Confirm/Cancel actions - use Pop Confirm, which is purpose-built for that exact pattern.
Content that should fully block the rest of the page - use Modal or Drawer instead of a lightweight anchored panel.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the content focused and scoped to what the trigger is about - a Popover shouldn't turn into a secondary page.
Close it on outside click and Escape, consistent with other floating-panel components.
Anchor it reliably to its trigger even as the page scrolls or resizes, so it never floats disconnected from context.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Storage almost full

92% used. Free up space or upgrade your plan.

ⓘ

A short title plus one or two lines of real detail - richer than a Tooltip, but still small enough to read at a glance.

DON'T

Account settings

Full profile editing, notification preferences, connected apps, billing history and two-factor setup all live here - update anything and it saves immediately across every device you are signed into.

ⓘ

A popover this dense is really a page pretending to float. Once it needs paragraphs, send the user to a real settings screen instead.

ACCESSIBILITY

The trigger exposes aria-expanded and aria-haspopup, reflecting the popover's open state.
Focus moves into the popover when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes.
Interactive content inside it (buttons, links) remains fully keyboard-reachable in a sensible tab order.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Tooltip, Pop Confirm, Dropdown.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Popover component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, content state, trigger label, title, body) - a rich floating content panel (title + optional body text + optional close button) anchored to a real clickable trigger button, opened on click (not hover, unlike this system's Tooltip component), not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Simple (a bold title line only); With body (the title plus a body paragraph below it, e.g. "Storage usage" / "8.2 GB of 15 GB used."); With close (title, body and a small "x" close button in the top-right corner of the bubble, for dismissing the popover without clicking outside it).

Visual treatment: the same inverted-overlay bubble as Tooltip/Tour/Pop Confirm - near-black in light theme, near-white in dark theme, via the fixed var(--overlay-invert-bg)/-text tokens (never the user-customizable var(--graphite-900)/var(--text-hi)), so it always contrasts with the page regardless of theme or any saved brand color. No border on the bubble - box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" (matching this system's other floating-panel language, Menu/Autocomplete) gives it enough separation from the page on its own; a border read as an unwanted outline against the inverted background. Reads as a proper elevated panel rather than Tooltip's flat single-line bubble, with border-radius var(--radius-md) and room for a title/body/close button. The trigger is a real clickable button (not a decorative circle like Tooltip's trigger), styled like a simple bordered button on the ordinary page background - background var(--graphite-800), border 1px solid var(--line-strong), color var(--text-hi), padding 8px 14px, border-radius var(--radius-sm) - since it sits outside the inverted bubble, not part of it. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)), same background as the bubble, with only half of it showing - the rest tucked behind the bubble's own opaque background as a clean triangular point (same technique as Tooltip's arrow).

Component properties: Trigger label (string, the text on the trigger button) - currently "Details". Title (string, bold text at the top of the bubble) - currently "Storage usage". Body (string, used by the With body and With close states) - currently "8.2 GB of 15 GB used.".

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Progress component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (layout, state, percent, show label) - a visual indicator of completion percentage, used for uploads, multi-step processes, loading operations, or any quantifiable completion state.

Layouts (2):
- Linear: a horizontal track with a fill bar that grows left-to-right to the current percent.
- Circular: a ring track with a fill arc that sweeps clockwise to the current percent.

States (3):
- In progress: uses the live Percent property value, filled in the accent color - represents an operation still running.
- Success: always shows 100% complete, filled in green - represents a finished operation, regardless of the Percent property.
- Error: always shows a fixed, partial value (40%), filled in a darker red with a diagonal hazard-stripe pattern (linear) or a dashed outline (circular) rather than a plain solid fill - represents a stalled or failed operation, visually distinct from the in-progress state even though both are red-family colors.

Component properties: Percent (0-100, default 66 - drives only the In progress state's fill), Show label (boolean, default on - shows the percentage as text alongside the bar or ring).

Accessibility: the track element (the one whose size represents 0-100%, not the wrapper or the fill) carries role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin="0", aria-valuemax="100", and aria-valuenow set to its current percent, plus an aria-label describing what it measures - so assistive technology can announce real progress, not just read a silent colored bar.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Progress component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (layout, state, percent, show label) - a visual indicator of completion percentage, used for uploads, multi-step processes, loading operations, or any quantifiable completion state.

Layouts (2):
- Linear: a horizontal track with a fill bar that grows left-to-right to the current percent.
- Circular: a ring track with a fill arc that sweeps clockwise to the current percent.

States (3):
- In progress: uses the live Percent property value, filled in the accent color - represents an operation still running.
- Success: always shows 100% complete, filled in green - represents a finished operation, regardless of the Percent property.
- Error: always shows a fixed, partial value (40%), filled in a darker red with a diagonal hazard-stripe pattern (linear) or a dashed outline (circular) rather than a plain solid fill - represents a stalled or failed operation, visually distinct from the in-progress state even though both are red-family colors.

Component properties: Percent (0-100, default 65 - drives only the In progress state's fill), Show label (boolean, default off - hides the percentage as text alongside the bar or ring).

Accessibility: the track element (the one whose size represents 0-100%, not the wrapper or the fill) carries role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin="0", aria-valuemax="100", and aria-valuenow set to its current percent, plus an aria-label describing what it measures - so assistive technology can announce real progress, not just read a silent colored bar.

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.
