OVERVIEW

Splitter is a resizable two-panel layout with a draggable divider between them - the user drags the divider to redistribute space between the two panels, and either panel can optionally collapse to a thin strip to temporarily reclaim its space.

WHEN TO USE

A resizable sidebar next to a main content area - a file tree, a navigation panel, or a filters panel.
A code editor and its live preview pane - both panels visible, resizable to taste.
A master/detail layout - a list panel and a detail panel, like a chat list next to a conversation pane.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A fixed layout where resizing adds no value - don't add a Splitter just because two things sit side by side; only when the user genuinely benefits from adjusting the ratio.
Narrow or mobile viewports - a draggable divider is impractical on touch-first layouts; stack the panels instead.
More than two panels needing independent resizing - nest multiple Splitters deliberately rather than trying to force one divider to manage three or more regions.

BEST PRACTICES

Persist the user's chosen split ratio across sessions when the layout is one they'll return to repeatedly.
Enforce sensible minimum sizes on both panels so neither can be dragged down to an unusable sliver.
Make the divider's hit target noticeably wider than its visible line, so it's easy to grab precisely.

DO AND DON'T

DO

File tree
Editor

Two panels the user genuinely wants to resize against each other, with a visible drag handle marking the boundary.

DON'T

Icons
Main content

A 15%-wide panel gives the user almost nothing to drag toward - there is no meaningful second layout to resize into. Use a fixed Sidebar instead.

ACCESSIBILITY

The divider is a real, keyboard-operable control (arrow keys nudge the split ratio), not a mouse-only drag handle.
The divider exposes its current position and valid range to assistive technology, similar to a slider.
A collapsed panel's expand control has an accessible name identifying which panel it restores.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Transfer, Card, Tabs.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Splitter component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, split ratio, state, panel content) - a two-panel layout separated by a draggable divider that lets the user redistribute space between the panels, not a one-off resize handle wired up per screen.

Types (2):
- Horizontal: panels sit side by side, divided by a vertical draggable line (col-resize cursor).
- Vertical: panels stack top to bottom, divided by a horizontal draggable line (row-resize cursor).

States (3):
- Default: a static split at the configured ratio (currently 35% / 65%).
- Dragging: the divider itself is highlighted (brand red) while the pointer is actively resizing - panel proportions mid-drag are whatever they were an instant before, not reset.
- Collapsed: the first panel shrinks to a thin 28px strip showing only an expand chevron, temporarily reclaiming its space for the second panel.

Component properties: First panel label (text, e.g. "Sidebar"); Second panel label (text, e.g. "Content"); Split ratio (number, percent given to the first panel when not collapsed) - currently 35.
Live interaction: include splitter-runtime.js and mount ADSSplitter. Named separator with arrow/Shift/Home/End/Enter keys, 64px minimum expanded panes, 10–90% bounds, collapse/restore, pointer cancellation and versioned width persistence. Use a unique storage key per product layout. Static state comparisons remain inert.

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Statistic component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, color, title, value, prefix, suffix) - a compact, high-emphasis display for a single quantifiable number, not a one-off big number hard-coded per dashboard tile.

Statistic is not interactive - it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is structural: 3 types, each in 4 states (which act as semantic colors, not interaction states).

Types (3):
- Default: a title above a large, bold value, with optional prefix/suffix.
- With Trend: same as Default, plus a small colored up/down arrow and a percentage change on its own line below the value.
- Countdown: same as Default, but the value renders in a monospace, timer-like style.

States (4, apply to every type):
- Default: neutral color (var(--text-hi)).
- Positive: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing up) in var(--green-500).
- Negative: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing down) in var(--danger-500).
- Loading: title stays visible, but the value is replaced by an animated shimmering placeholder bar - never show a stale or fake value while loading.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "AuditField42"); Value (text, e.g. "112,893"); Prefix (optional text shown immediately before the value, e.g. a currency symbol) - currently ""; Suffix (optional text shown immediately after the value, e.g. a unit or percent sign) - currently "".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Statistic component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, color, title, value, prefix, suffix) - a compact, high-emphasis display for a single quantifiable number, not a one-off big number hard-coded per dashboard tile.

Statistic is not interactive - it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is structural: 3 types, each in 4 states (which act as semantic colors, not interaction states).

Types (3):
- Default: a title above a large, bold value, with optional prefix/suffix.
- With Trend: same as Default, plus a small colored up/down arrow and a percentage change on its own line below the value.
- Countdown: same as Default, but the value renders in a monospace, timer-like style.

States (4, apply to every type):
- Default: neutral color (var(--text-hi)).
- Positive: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing up) in var(--green-500).
- Negative: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing down) in var(--danger-500).
- Loading: title stays visible, but the value is replaced by an animated shimmering placeholder bar - never show a stale or fake value while loading.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Active Users"); Value (text, e.g. "AuditField42"); Prefix (optional text shown immediately before the value, e.g. a currency symbol) - currently ""; Suffix (optional text shown immediately after the value, e.g. a unit or percent sign) - currently "".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Statistic component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, color, title, value, prefix, suffix) - a compact, high-emphasis display for a single quantifiable number, not a one-off big number hard-coded per dashboard tile.

Statistic is not interactive - it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is structural: 3 types, each in 4 states (which act as semantic colors, not interaction states).

Types (3):
- Default: a title above a large, bold value, with optional prefix/suffix.
- With Trend: same as Default, plus a small colored up/down arrow and a percentage change on its own line below the value.
- Countdown: same as Default, but the value renders in a monospace, timer-like style.

States (4, apply to every type):
- Default: neutral color (var(--text-hi)).
- Positive: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing up) in var(--green-500).
- Negative: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing down) in var(--danger-500).
- Loading: title stays visible, but the value is replaced by an animated shimmering placeholder bar - never show a stale or fake value while loading.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Active Users"); Value (text, e.g. "112,893"); Prefix (optional text shown immediately before the value, e.g. a currency symbol) - currently "AuditField42"; Suffix (optional text shown immediately after the value, e.g. a unit or percent sign) - currently "".

Create a complete Statistic component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, color, title, value, prefix, suffix) - a compact, high-emphasis display for a single quantifiable number, not a one-off big number hard-coded per dashboard tile.

Statistic is not interactive - it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is structural: 3 types, each in 4 states (which act as semantic colors, not interaction states).

Types (3):
- Default: a title above a large, bold value, with optional prefix/suffix.
- With Trend: same as Default, plus a small colored up/down arrow and a percentage change on its own line below the value.
- Countdown: same as Default, but the value renders in a monospace, timer-like style.

States (4, apply to every type):
- Default: neutral color (var(--text-hi)).
- Positive: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing up) in var(--green-500).
- Negative: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing down) in var(--danger-500).
- Loading: title stays visible, but the value is replaced by an animated shimmering placeholder bar - never show a stale or fake value while loading.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Active Users"); Value (text, e.g. "112,893"); Prefix (optional text shown immediately before the value, e.g. a currency symbol) - currently ""; Suffix (optional text shown immediately after the value, e.g. a unit or percent sign) - currently "AuditField42".

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Active Users"); Value (text, e.g. "112,893"); Prefix (optional text shown immediately before the value, e.g. a currency symbol) - currently ""; Suffix (optional text shown immediately after the value, e.g. a unit or percent sign) - currently "".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

OVERVIEW

Statistic displays a single quantifiable number prominently - a title above a large, bold value, with an optional prefix (like a currency symbol), suffix (like a unit or percent sign), and a colored trend indicator - built for dashboard tiles and summary cards where one number needs to stand out at a glance.

WHEN TO USE

A dashboard KPI tile - active users, total revenue, open tickets.
A metric with a trend - growth or decline versus a prior period, shown with a colored arrow.
A live counter or a countdown - a value that updates over time but is always shown as one prominent number.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Several related numbers that need to be compared side by side in rows and columns - use Table or Description instead of several standalone Statistic tiles.
A number the user needs to edit - use Number or Input; Statistic is read-only, display-only.
A value with no real numeric significance - a plain label or Tag communicates a status better than dressing it up as a number.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the title short and unambiguous - a viewer should know exactly what the number represents without extra context.
Format large numbers with separators (112,893, not 112893) so they're readable at a glance - use the locale-correct separator from Data Format rather than hard-coding a comma, since Statistic itself doesn't define number formatting.
Reserve the positive/negative trend coloring for values that are genuinely good or bad news - don't color a neutral count green or red by default.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Monthly active users

48,204
▲ 12%

One number, labelled plainly, with the trend that gives it meaning - up from what, and by how much.

DON'T

Users

48,204.37

Raw unrounded precision on a headline number reads as noise, not confidence - it forces the reader to mentally truncate it themselves.

ACCESSIBILITY

The title and value are both real text, read together by screen readers as one meaningful statement, not conveyed by size or color alone.
Trend direction is stated in text or via an icon with an accessible label ("up 12.5%"), not communicated by arrow shape or color alone.
The loading state is marked so assistive technology announces that the value is not yet available, rather than reading an empty placeholder.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Description, Progress, Badge.

Create a complete Statistic component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, color, title, value, prefix, suffix) - a compact, high-emphasis display for a single quantifiable number, not a one-off big number hard-coded per dashboard tile.

Statistic is not interactive - it has no hover, focus or disabled state. Its variation is structural: 3 types, each in 4 states (which act as semantic colors, not interaction states).

Types (3):
- Default: a title above a large, bold value, with optional prefix/suffix.
- With Trend: same as Default, plus a small colored up/down arrow and a percentage change on its own line below the value.
- Countdown: same as Default, but the value renders in a monospace, timer-like style.

States (4, apply to every type):
- Default: neutral color (var(--text-hi)).
- Positive: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing up) in var(--green-500).
- Negative: value (and, for With Trend, the arrow pointing down) in var(--danger-500).
- Loading: title stays visible, but the value is replaced by an animated shimmering placeholder bar - never show a stale or fake value while loading.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Active Users"); Value (text, e.g. "112,893"); Prefix (optional text shown immediately before the value, e.g. a currency symbol) - currently ""; Suffix (optional text shown immediately after the value, e.g. a unit or percent sign) - currently "".

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment, Step 4" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "AuditField42" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

Orientation: Vertical - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

Orientation: Horizontal - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

Size: 32px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

Size: 40px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

Orientation: Horizontal - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

Size: 24px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

Orientation: Horizontal - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

Size: 24px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

title: Steps STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Steps (progress indicator) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(15,15,10,0.15) border, transparent fill), step number in #69707D, connector lines on both sides in rgba(15,15,10,0.15).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #111827 and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(15,15,10,0.15) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

OVERVIEW

Steps shows position within a multi-step flow, like a checkout or onboarding wizard - numbered circles connected by a line, each marked completed, current, or upcoming, so the user always knows how far along they are and what's left. Runs horizontal (left to right) or vertical (top to bottom, circle beside its label) via the Orientation property.

WHEN TO USE

A checkout flow - Details, Shipping, Payment.
An onboarding wizard or multi-page form - showing progress across a fixed sequence.
Setup progress - a guided configuration flow with a known number of stages.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A set of related but independent views with no required order - use Tabs instead, since Steps implies a strict sequence.
A location within a nested hierarchy rather than a linear sequence - use Breadcrumb.
A flow with an unknown or highly variable number of stages - Steps works best with a fixed, known step count; consider Progress instead if the total isn't fixed.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep step labels short and in plain, parallel language ("Details", "Shipping", "Payment").
Let users navigate back to a completed step when the flow allows revisiting earlier choices.
Reflect real progress accurately - never mark a step completed before its content has actually been filled in or confirmed.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, orientation, size, labels, per-step status) - a row showing position within a multi-step flow like checkout or onboarding, not separate one-off labels glued together. Steps are inherently sequential: every step before the current one renders as completed, every step after it renders as upcoming.

Type: Numbered - Each step is a circle containing its number, or a checkmark icon once that step is completed - the clearest option when steps benefit from an at-a-glance count.

States (5, apply per step):
- Upcoming: empty ring (1.5px rgba(255,255,255,0.16) border, transparent fill), step number in #7F8694, connector lines on both sides in rgba(255,255,255,0.16).
- Current: solid #FF031A background, step number in white (never a checkmark - that's Completed only), label text in #D8DFEE and bold.
- Completed: solid #FF031A background with a checkmark icon in white in place of the number, connector line after it in rgba(255,255,255,0.16) (the next step is upcoming) but the connector before it in #FF031A (the previous step is completed too).
- Error: solid #ff031a background with an X mark in white, label text in #ff031a.
- Disabled: empty ring at 40% opacity, label text at 40% opacity - static/illustrative, not interactive.
- A connector is only filled (brand red) when both steps it joins are completed; otherwise it stays the neutral line color.

What orientation do you want? (Horizontal / Vertical) Horizontal runs left-to-right with the circle above its label and a horizontal connector between circles; Vertical stacks top-to-bottom with the circle beside its label and a vertical connector below each circle, centered under the circle column either way.

What size do you want? (24px - S / 32px - M / 40px - L) Circle diameter and the number/icon size scale together, applied to every step.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per step, current value "Details, Shipping, Payment" - step count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Switch (toggle) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a pill-shaped track with a sliding circular thumb that flips a single setting on or off, not a checkbox merely styled to look like one.

Types (2):
- Compact: Just the toggle itself, with no visible text label - use where the surrounding context already explains what's being toggled, like a table row or a toolbar.
- Labeled: Toggle plus a text label to its right - use as a standalone control where the setting needs its own visible name, like a settings panel.

States (5, same visual treatment for both types):
- Off: background:#e3e3df; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb sits at the left.
- On: background:#FF031A; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb slides to the right.
- Hover: background:#c7c7c1 (off-state only).
- Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253; outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so the focus ring stays visible against every other state.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; cursor:not-allowed;

What size do you want? (20px - S / 24px - M / 32px - L) Track width scales with height (width = height x 1.75, rounded); thumb size and travel distance scale with it too.

Component properties: Label (editable text next to the switch, shown for the Labeled type and used as the accessible name for both).

Create a complete Switch (toggle) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a pill-shaped track with a sliding circular thumb that flips a single setting on or off, not a checkbox merely styled to look like one.

Types (2):
- Compact: Just the toggle itself, with no visible text label - use where the surrounding context already explains what's being toggled, like a table row or a toolbar.
- Labeled: Toggle plus a text label to its right - use as a standalone control where the setting needs its own visible name, like a settings panel.

States (5, same visual treatment for both types):
- Off: background:#e3e3df; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb sits at the left.
- On: background:#FF031A; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb slides to the right.
- Hover: background:#c7c7c1 (off-state only).
- Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253; outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so the focus ring stays visible against every other state.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; cursor:not-allowed;

Size: 20px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Track width scales with height (width = height x 1.75, rounded); thumb size and travel distance scale with it too.

Component properties: Label (editable text next to the switch, shown for the Labeled type and used as the accessible name for both).

Create a complete Switch (toggle) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a pill-shaped track with a sliding circular thumb that flips a single setting on or off, not a checkbox merely styled to look like one.

Types (2):
- Compact: Just the toggle itself, with no visible text label - use where the surrounding context already explains what's being toggled, like a table row or a toolbar.
- Labeled: Toggle plus a text label to its right - use as a standalone control where the setting needs its own visible name, like a settings panel.

States (5, same visual treatment for both types):
- Off: background:#e3e3df; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb sits at the left.
- On: background:#FF031A; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb slides to the right.
- Hover: background:#c7c7c1 (off-state only).
- Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253; outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so the focus ring stays visible against every other state.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; cursor:not-allowed;

What size do you want? (20px - S / 24px - M / 32px - L) Track width scales with height (width = height x 1.75, rounded); thumb size and travel distance scale with it too.

Component properties: Label (editable text next to the switch, shown for the Labeled type and used as the accessible name for both).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Switch (toggle) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, state) - a pill-shaped track with a sliding circular thumb that flips a single setting on or off, not a checkbox merely styled to look like one.

Types (2):
- Compact: Just the toggle itself, with no visible text label - use where the surrounding context already explains what's being toggled, like a table row or a toolbar.
- Labeled: Toggle plus a text label to its right - use as a standalone control where the setting needs its own visible name, like a settings panel.

States (5, same visual treatment for both types):
- Off: background:#e3e3df; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb sits at the left.
- On: background:#FF031A; thumb background:#FFFFFF, thumb slides to the right.
- Hover: background:#c7c7c1 (off-state only).
- Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253; outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so the focus ring stays visible against every other state.
- Disabled: opacity:0.4; cursor:not-allowed;

Size: 32px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Track width scales with height (width = height x 1.75, rounded); thumb size and travel distance scale with it too.

Component properties: Label (editable text next to the switch, shown for the Labeled type and used as the accessible name for both).
