Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Large - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Middle - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

title: Table STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

No results

Try a different search or filter.

When to use

Any time structured data needs to be shown across fixed columns rather than as a list or grid of cards.

Admin data grid
User management list
Order history
Report/analytics view
Inventory listing
Selection

Row selection is one of three modes per table instance, not a single on/off switch - pick the one that matches what an action needs to operate on.

None - rows aren't selectable. No checkbox column, no row highlight on click; a click (if it does anything) navigates or expands the row instead of selecting it.
Single-row - clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group: selecting a different row clears the previous selection. Use when exactly one record is ever acted on at a time.
Multi-row (checkbox column) - a leading checkbox column: one checkbox per row, plus a header checkbox that selects or deselects every row currently visible. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox renders indeterminate - a dash, not a checkmark or an empty box - rather than falsely claiming everything or nothing is selected.

Keyboard: a selectable row is a focusable element (tabindex="0"); pressing Space while a row has focus toggles that row's selection, without requiring the pointer to land precisely on the checkbox.

Sort

Sorting can happen entirely in the browser or round-trip to the server, depending on how much of the dataset is already loaded.

Client-side sort - re-orders rows already loaded in memory. Fine for small, fully-loaded datasets where every row is already on the page.
Server-side sort - re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change. Required once pagination or virtualization is itself server-driven, so sorting one column doesn't mean silently fetching the entire dataset just to reorder it locally.
Multi-column sort - single-column sort is the default; supporting a secondary sort key (e.g. shift-click a header to add it) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not something every Table instance is required to implement.

Accessibility contract - per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable column header must expose its current state via aria-sort="ascending", aria-sort="descending" or aria-sort="none" on the <th>, update that attribute the instant the sort changes, and announce the change to assistive technology - a visual arrow icon alone is not sufficient.

Filter

Filtering narrows which rows show, through either a scoped per-column control or a single global search - and the resulting empty state needs to say which situation it is.

Per-column filter - a control scoped to one field, e.g. a status dropdown inside the Status column's header, narrowing on that attribute alone.
Global search bar - one search input above the table that matches across every visible column at once, for a user who doesn't know which column their query lives in.

"No rows match" is not the same empty state as "no data at all." A filtered-to-zero result (rows exist, the current filter or search just matched none of them) should say so and offer a "Clear filters" action; the true empty state (no data exists, prior to any filter) should instead offer a call-to-action to create the first record. Rendering the same message for both hides the fact that data exists somewhere but the filter is too narrow.

Pagination vs. Virtualization

A Table doesn't scale linearly in the DOM as row count grows, so which rendering strategy applies depends on how many rows are in play.

Below 500 rows - client-side pagination, or simply rendering every row at once, is fine. The DOM cost is small and bounded.
At or above 500 rows - virtualization (windowed rendering, where only the rows in or near the current viewport are ever mounted) is required. A table row is not a cheap DOM node - each one carries multiple cells, and often interactive controls (checkboxes, action buttons) with their own event listeners - so total DOM node count and layout/reflow cost grow far faster than linearly with row count once a table passes a few hundred rows.
Density

A two-value row-height property, independent of the Size property already shown above in Live Preview.

Comfortable - the default row height and cell padding, matching what's shown throughout this page's Live Preview.
Compact - reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows within the same viewport height.

A sitewide density mode now exists (Settings → Density, backed by a data-density attribute the same way theme is), but Table's Size property above is still its own local control and isn't wired to that sitewide setting yet - the two aren't the same switch. Promote Table's Size onto the sitewide toggle once another data-dense component (List, Description) needs the same switch, rather than each maintaining its own.

Required States

A real, data-backed Table has no fallback "shape" the way this page's static demos do - empty, loading and error all need an explicit, intentional rendering, not an accidental one.

Showing the same "No results" empty state while a fetch is still in flight misreports that there's no data - rows popping in a moment later contradicts what was just displayed.

OVERVIEW

Table displays structured data across fixed columns, like an admin data grid or a report view - rows and columns that let a user compare values across many records at once, unlike List's simpler stacked-row layout with no column alignment.

WHEN TO USE

An admin data grid or user management list - structured records compared across shared columns.
Order history or a report/analytics view - tabular data where column alignment aids comparison.
An inventory listing - any dataset naturally organized into consistent fields per row.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A simple stack of similar items with no meaningful column structure - use List instead - Table's column overhead isn't worth it for unstructured rows.
A small number of visually distinct content blocks - use Card or a grid of Cards.
Data better suited to a single set of label/value pairs - use Description for one record's details rather than a one-row table.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep column headers concise and consistently aligned with their column's data type (numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned).
Support sorting on columns where order genuinely helps comparison, and clearly indicate the active sort.
Pair large tables with pagination, virtualized scrolling, or both - virtualize once a table is showing 500+ rows, rather than rendering thousands of rows at once.

DO AND DON'T

ACCESSIBILITY

Uses real table semantics (thead/tbody/th with proper scope), so screen readers can announce row/column context for each cell.
Sortable column headers are real, keyboard-operable buttons that announce the current sort direction.
Row selection checkboxes are independently labeled with which row they apply to.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "AuditField42" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

Size: 28px - XS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

Size: 32px - S - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

Size: 36px - SM - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

Size: 44px - L - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.

  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Tabs (tab bar) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - a horizontal row of tab triggers where exactly one is active at a time. Only the tab bar itself, not a full page with panel content underneath.

Types (2):
- Underline: A minimal bar where the active tab gets a 2px accent underline and no background change - reads as part of the page's own text hierarchy, not a separate control.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;
  Active: color:#111827;border-bottom:2px solid #FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
- Pill: A solid pill highlight follows the active tab - useful when the tab bar needs to stand out as its own control, separate from the page content around it.
  Rest: background:transparent;color:#4B5563;
  Active: background:rgba(255,3,26,0.08);color:#FF031A;font-weight:600;
  Hover: background:#f1f1ee;color:#111827;
  Focused: outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.

States (4, apply per trigger): Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled.
- Exactly one trigger is Active at all times - a separate property from these four states, so the bar always shows realistic always-one-selected context.
- Disabled applies to one trigger at a time (its own real disabled attribute, 40% opacity, not-allowed cursor), not the whole bar.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. This is the tab bar's height - padding and font-size scale proportionally, applied to every trigger.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Only visually affects the Pill type's active tab (its pill background) - the Underline type ignores it entirely.

Component properties: Labels (comma-separated editable text, one per trigger, current value "Overview, Activity, Settings" - trigger count follows the number of labels entered).
