Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 24px - XXS - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 8px - Balanced - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

Size: 40px - M - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

title: Time STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focused: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Validation

Typed time entry can be malformed or simply out of range, and a picker-selected value can still fall outside a business-hours-style limit - both need direct, specific feedback.

Required marking - mark the field required only when a time value is mandatory to proceed, with the standard label asterisk.
Validation timing - validate typed entry on blur, not on every keystroke, so a partial entry like "9:3" isn't flagged mid-type. A picker-selected value is validated immediately, since the picker only offers valid options.
Invalid time entry - reject an out-of-range or malformed value with a specific message - "Hours must be between 00 and 23," "Minutes must be between 00 and 59," or, for a format mismatch like "930" instead of "9:30," ask for the expected format directly.
Allowed range - if the field is limited to a window (e.g. business hours only), reject a time outside it with a specific message like "Choose a time between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM," and gray out out-of-range options in the picker itself so most invalid picks are prevented rather than only caught after entry.
Error message - show the message inline next to the field, worded specifically enough that the user knows exactly what to change.
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Time is a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon that opens a time picker for selecting a time of day - the temporal counterpart to Date Picker, used whenever the value is a time rather than a calendar date.

WHEN TO USE

A meeting or event start time - any specific time of day.
A reminder or alarm - a time with no associated calendar date.
Store hours or an appointment slot - a time chosen from within a day.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A calendar date - use Date Picker.
Both a date and a time together - pair Date Picker and Time as two fields, or use a combined date-time pattern if the product defines one - Time alone doesn't carry a date.
A duration rather than a point in time - e.g. "2 hours" - use Number with a unit label instead.

BEST PRACTICES

Respect the user's locale for 12-hour vs. 24-hour display, rather than hard-coding one format.
Snap the picker to a sensible interval (e.g. 15 minutes) when exact-to-the-second precision isn't meaningful.
Let the user type a time directly as an alternative to scrolling/clicking through the picker.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Meeting starts
09:30

Your local time (GMT+1).

Names the timezone the number is in, which is the only thing that makes a time shared between people actionable.

DON'T

Meeting starts
09:30

A bare time is ambiguous the moment two people in different places read it, and neither of them will notice until one misses the meeting.

ACCESSIBILITY

The time picker is fully keyboard-operable (arrow keys or typing to adjust hour/minute, Enter to confirm).
The field's accessible name states what the time represents ("Meeting start time"), not just "Time".
AM/PM (in 12-hour format) is exposed as its own clearly labeled control, not bundled invisibly into the hour value.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Date Picker, Date Range, Number.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Time component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant. It is visually a text field with a fixed trailing clock icon (not a leading icon, to match Select's chevron placement convention) and no visible text cursor, since its value is set via a time-selection UI rather than typed character-by-character. Scope is the trigger control itself, in all its states - the trigger opens a time-selection UI on click/focus in a real implementation, but that popup UI is not built out here, the same "declared but not interactively simulated" convention Date Picker itself already uses for its calendar popup.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default time field style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#15171a;border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
  Hover: border-color:#7F8694;
  Focused: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#1c1f23;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#262a2f;
  Focused: background:#15171a;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Error: border-color:#ff031a; Paired with an inline error message below the field in #ff031a.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focused, Filled, Error, Disabled.
- Filled: same appearance as Rest, showing the selected time value (e.g. 10:30 AM) instead of the placeholder.
- Error: pairs with an inline error message below the field.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Placeholder (editable text shown when no time is chosen, e.g. "Select a time").

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Timeline component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (layout, state, show icons) - a vertical list of chronological events, each with a dot (or optional status icon) connected by a continuous vertical line, used for activity logs, order status history, or a project's milestone history.

Layouts (3):
- Default: dots aligned to the left, with every event's title and timestamp to the right of the connecting line, stacked vertically.
- Alternate: dots centered on the line, with event content alternating left and right of it for odd/even events - a classic alternating vertical timeline layout.
- Horizontal: events flow left to right along a single horizontal line, with each dot centered above its own title and timestamp.

States (3):
- Default: plain, neutral-colored dots (or icons) - every event reads as complete/neutral, with no emphasis on any one item.
- With events: the same events, but the current/in-progress event (the second one) gets an accent-colored dot and a bolder title, so it stands out from the events around it.
- Pending: the same events plus a trailing, dimmed placeholder item with a dashed segment of connecting line above it and no timestamp (just "Pending..."), indicating more events are still to come.

Component properties: Show icons (boolean, default off) - ON, so every dot is replaced with a small colored status icon (a checkmark in a circle). The current event in the "With events" state and the pending placeholder keep their own accent/dimmed coloring regardless of this setting.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

title: Timeline STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Timeline component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (layout, state, show icons) - a vertical list of chronological events, each with a dot (or optional status icon) connected by a continuous vertical line, used for activity logs, order status history, or a project's milestone history.

Layouts (3):
- Default: dots aligned to the left, with every event's title and timestamp to the right of the connecting line, stacked vertically.
- Alternate: dots centered on the line, with event content alternating left and right of it for odd/even events - a classic alternating vertical timeline layout.
- Horizontal: events flow left to right along a single horizontal line, with each dot centered above its own title and timestamp.

States (3):
- Default: plain, neutral-colored dots (or icons) - every event reads as complete/neutral, with no emphasis on any one item.
- With events: the same events, but the current/in-progress event (the second one) gets an accent-colored dot and a bolder title, so it stands out from the events around it.
- Pending: the same events plus a trailing, dimmed placeholder item with a dashed segment of connecting line above it and no timestamp (just "Pending..."), indicating more events are still to come.

Component properties: Show icons (boolean, default off) - OFF, so every event shows a plain dot rather than an icon. The current event in the "With events" state and the pending placeholder keep their own accent/dimmed coloring regardless of this setting.

Component Guide

OVERVIEW

Timeline shows a sequence of events in chronological order, each with a dot connected by a continuous line - used for activity logs, order status history, or a project's milestone history, so the reader can see what happened, when, and in what order.

WHEN TO USE

Order status history - showing each stage a shipment or order has passed through.
An activity or audit log - chronological events tied to a record.
Project milestone tracking or onboarding progress - a sequence of events, each with a point in time.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A fixed sequence the user is actively moving through right now - use Steps instead - Timeline is a historical record, Steps is an in-progress flow.
Unordered or non-chronological content - a Timeline's core value is chronological order; don't use it for a list with no meaningful sequence.
A simple list with no time dimension at all - use List.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep each entry's timestamp visible and consistently formatted, since chronology is the whole point of a Timeline.
Use distinct icons or colors sparingly, reserved for genuinely different event types, not decoration.
For very long histories, consider collapsing older entries or paginating rather than rendering the entire history at once.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Order shipped

14 Mar, 09:12

Out for delivery

Expected 16 Mar

Events in chronological order, each with a timestamp, so the sequence and its pacing are both readable.

DON'T

Out for delivery

Order shipped

Events out of order with no timestamps leave the reader unable to tell what actually happened when - the one thing a timeline exists to show.

ACCESSIBILITY

Each entry's timestamp and description are real text, read in order by screen readers, not implied only by visual position on the line.
The connecting line and dots are decorative and hidden from assistive technology - the meaningful content is the entry text itself.
Event type (success, error, pending) is distinguishable by more than color, using an icon or text label as well.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Steps, List, Result.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Timeline component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (layout, state, show icons) - a vertical list of chronological events, each with a dot (or optional status icon) connected by a continuous vertical line, used for activity logs, order status history, or a project's milestone history.

Layouts (3):
- Default: dots aligned to the left, with every event's title and timestamp to the right of the connecting line, stacked vertically.
- Alternate: dots centered on the line, with event content alternating left and right of it for odd/even events - a classic alternating vertical timeline layout.
- Horizontal: events flow left to right along a single horizontal line, with each dot centered above its own title and timestamp.

States (3):
- Default: plain, neutral-colored dots (or icons) - every event reads as complete/neutral, with no emphasis on any one item.
- With events: the same events, but the current/in-progress event (the second one) gets an accent-colored dot and a bolder title, so it stands out from the events around it.
- Pending: the same events plus a trailing, dimmed placeholder item with a dashed segment of connecting line above it and no timestamp (just "Pending..."), indicating more events are still to come.

Component properties: Show icons (boolean, default off) - OFF, so every event shows a plain dot rather than an icon. The current event in the "With events" state and the pending placeholder keep their own accent/dimmed coloring regardless of this setting.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "AuditField42", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;

- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.

Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.
