Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).

title: Toast STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#fbfbfa;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

Upload confirmation
Action undo prompt
Background job complete
Copy-to-clipboard confirmation
Connection status change
Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Toast is a temporary, floating confirmation of an action or status change, typically surfaced in a fixed screen corner rather than embedded inline like Alert - it appears, communicates its message, and disappears on its own without requiring the user to stay put.

WHEN TO USE

A brief confirmation after an action - upload complete, copy-to-clipboard confirmation.
An undo prompt - a short window to reverse the action just taken.
A background job completing or a connection status change - events the user doesn't need to actively wait for.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A message that needs to stay visible until manually dismissed or resolved - use Alert, which is embedded and persistent, not self-dismissing.
Anything requiring a decision before the user can continue - use Modal or Pop Confirm - a self-dismissing Toast is the wrong place for a choice with consequences.
Detailed or long-form content - use Notification, which is built for a longer title/description pairing.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the message short enough to read in the few seconds before it disappears.
Stack multiple toasts rather than replacing one before the user has had a chance to read it.
Give an undo action a genuinely sufficient window before the toast dismisses, if undo is offered at all.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Draft saved

Short enough to read in the couple of seconds it is on screen, confirming something the user just did.

DON'T

Delete this workspace?

This removes all 240 files permanently.

A decision inside a toast can vanish before it is answered. Anything with consequences belongs in a Modal or Pop Confirm.

ACCESSIBILITY

Announced via an aria-live region so screen-reader users are told about it without needing to be focused on it.
Long enough on-screen duration (or a pause-on-hover/focus behavior) so it doesn't disappear before it can be read or acted on.
Any inline action (like Undo) is a real, independently focusable control.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Alert, Notification, Result.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Toast (floating notification) component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state, radius) - a floating, elevated notification card (solid background, border, drop shadow, fixed ~340px max-width) that appears temporarily to confirm an action or report a status.

It differs from Alert by being a floating overlay element, not inline page content - in production it is typically rendered in a fixed screen corner (e.g. bottom-right), stacked above the page, rather than embedded in the content flow the way Alert is.

Types (4, drive only the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational status update - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Icon color: color:#4f8fe6;
- Success: Confirms an action completed successfully. Icon color: color:#2fbf6e;
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Icon color: color:#e6a53a;
- Error: Reports that an action failed. Icon color: color:#ff031a;
Card (same for every type): background:#191c20;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);

States (4, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: title and description only, no extra controls.
- Dismissible: adds a trailing close (x) icon button in the card's top-right corner.
- With action: adds an inline text-style action button (e.g. "View") below the description.
- With progress: adds a thin colored progress/timer bar along the card's bottom edge, using the type's accent color at roughly 60% width to suggest a countdown in progress.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applied to the whole card, with matching inset on the bottom edge so the With-progress bar never pokes out past rounded corners.

Component properties: Title (text, default "Upload complete"); Description (text, default "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully."); Show icon (boolean toggle, default on - shows the semantic type icon beside the title/description).
Current values - Title: "Upload complete", Description: "your-file.pdf was uploaded successfully.", Show icon: yes.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Tooltip component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, size, content state) - a small floating label anchored to a trigger element on one of 4 sides, with a connecting arrow, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Plain text (a single line of text only); Rich (a bold title line plus a smaller description line below it, e.g. "Keyboard shortcut" / "Press Cmd+K to open"); Long text (wraps to 2-3 lines at a max-width around 180px instead of forcing the bubble wider).

Visual treatment: one consistent look regardless of placement or content state - this is a neutral utility component, not semantically colored like Alert or Toast. Inverted against the page (near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme - background var(--overlay-invert-bg), color var(--overlay-invert-text), NOT the normal-surface var(--text-hi)/var(--graphite-900) pair, since those are user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the guaranteed inversion), the arrow a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) in the same background color, positioned so it visually connects the bubble to the trigger.

Component properties: Size (Small/Default/Large, controls padding and font-size) - currently Small (4px 8px padding, 11px font). Show arrow (boolean, toggles the connecting arrow) - currently shown. Text content (string, used by the Plain text state) - currently "Add to favorites".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Tooltip component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, size, content state) - a small floating label anchored to a trigger element on one of 4 sides, with a connecting arrow, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Plain text (a single line of text only); Rich (a bold title line plus a smaller description line below it, e.g. "Keyboard shortcut" / "Press Cmd+K to open"); Long text (wraps to 2-3 lines at a max-width around 180px instead of forcing the bubble wider).

Visual treatment: one consistent look regardless of placement or content state - this is a neutral utility component, not semantically colored like Alert or Toast. Inverted against the page (near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme - background var(--overlay-invert-bg), color var(--overlay-invert-text), NOT the normal-surface var(--text-hi)/var(--graphite-900) pair, since those are user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the guaranteed inversion), the arrow a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) in the same background color, positioned so it visually connects the bubble to the trigger.

Component properties: Size (Small/Default/Large, controls padding and font-size) - currently Large (8px 12px padding, 13px font). Show arrow (boolean, toggles the connecting arrow) - currently shown. Text content (string, used by the Plain text state) - currently "Add to favorites".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Tooltip component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, size, content state) - a small floating label anchored to a trigger element on one of 4 sides, with a connecting arrow, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Plain text (a single line of text only); Rich (a bold title line plus a smaller description line below it, e.g. "Keyboard shortcut" / "Press Cmd+K to open"); Long text (wraps to 2-3 lines at a max-width around 180px instead of forcing the bubble wider).

Visual treatment: one consistent look regardless of placement or content state - this is a neutral utility component, not semantically colored like Alert or Toast. Inverted against the page (near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme - background var(--overlay-invert-bg), color var(--overlay-invert-text), NOT the normal-surface var(--text-hi)/var(--graphite-900) pair, since those are user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the guaranteed inversion), the arrow a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) in the same background color, positioned so it visually connects the bubble to the trigger.

Component properties: Size (Small/Default/Large, controls padding and font-size) - currently Default (6px 10px padding, 12px font). Show arrow (boolean, toggles the connecting arrow) - currently shown. Text content (string, used by the Plain text state) - currently "AuditField42".

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Tooltip component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, size, content state) - a small floating label anchored to a trigger element on one of 4 sides, with a connecting arrow, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Plain text (a single line of text only); Rich (a bold title line plus a smaller description line below it, e.g. "Keyboard shortcut" / "Press Cmd+K to open"); Long text (wraps to 2-3 lines at a max-width around 180px instead of forcing the bubble wider).

Visual treatment: one consistent look regardless of placement or content state - this is a neutral utility component, not semantically colored like Alert or Toast. Inverted against the page (near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme - background var(--overlay-invert-bg), color var(--overlay-invert-text), NOT the normal-surface var(--text-hi)/var(--graphite-900) pair, since those are user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the guaranteed inversion), the arrow a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) in the same background color, positioned so it visually connects the bubble to the trigger.

Component properties: Size (Small/Default/Large, controls padding and font-size) - currently Default (6px 10px padding, 12px font). Show arrow (boolean, toggles the connecting arrow) - currently hidden. Text content (string, used by the Plain text state) - currently "Add to favorites".

- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1

title: Tooltip STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Tooltip component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, size, content state) - a small floating label anchored to a trigger element on one of 4 sides, with a connecting arrow, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the bubble sits on the given side of the trigger, with a small arrow connecting it back to the trigger. Top's arrow points down at the trigger below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the trigger above it, Left's arrow points right at the trigger beside it, Right's arrow points left at the trigger beside it.

Content states (3): Plain text (a single line of text only); Rich (a bold title line plus a smaller description line below it, e.g. "Keyboard shortcut" / "Press Cmd+K to open"); Long text (wraps to 2-3 lines at a max-width around 180px instead of forcing the bubble wider).

Visual treatment: one consistent look regardless of placement or content state - this is a neutral utility component, not semantically colored like Alert or Toast. Inverted against the page (near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme - background var(--overlay-invert-bg), color var(--overlay-invert-text), NOT the normal-surface var(--text-hi)/var(--graphite-900) pair, since those are user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the guaranteed inversion), the arrow a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) in the same background color, positioned so it visually connects the bubble to the trigger.

Component properties: Size (Small/Default/Large, controls padding and font-size) - currently Default (6px 10px padding, 12px font). Show arrow (boolean, toggles the connecting arrow) - currently shown. Text content (string, used by the Plain text state) - currently "Add to favorites".

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Component Guide
Human View
Machine View

OVERVIEW

Tooltip adds a short hint next to a trigger element, like an icon-only button, without needing to click anything - a small floating label that appears on hover or focus and disappears when attention moves elsewhere.

WHEN TO USE

Labeling an icon-only control - explaining what an unlabeled icon button does.
Disclosing truncated text - showing the full value of text cut off with an ellipsis.
A keyboard shortcut hint or a brief explanation for a disabled control - why an action currently can't be taken.

WHEN NOT TO USE

Essential information the user must see to complete a task - hover-only content is easy to miss, especially on touch devices; put critical information visibly on screen instead.
Long or multi-paragraph content - use Popover, which supports richer content and stays open until dismissed.
Content that needs to remain visible while the user interacts with it - a tooltip disappears when hover/focus moves away, so it can't hold interactive controls of its own.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the text to a single short phrase or sentence - if it needs more, use Popover instead.
Trigger it on both hover and keyboard focus, never hover alone, so keyboard users get the same information.
Avoid delaying its appearance so long that it feels unresponsive, or so little that it flickers on incidental mouse movement.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Archive
□

Supplies the name of an icon-only control - exactly the gap a tooltip exists to fill.

DON'T

Required. Must be 8+ characters with a number and a symbol.
□

Rules the user needs while typing should not be hidden behind hover - they are invisible on touch and gone the moment the pointer moves. Put them in the field's help text.

ACCESSIBILITY

Associated with its trigger via aria-describedby pointing at the tooltip bubble's id, so screen readers announce it as supplementary information about the focused control, not as an unrelated interruption.

Never the only source of essential information - it must supplement, not replace, a visible accessible name.

Create a complete Tour component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, step-position state, target label, title, description) - a step-by-step walkthrough card (title + description + step counter + Back/Next or Back/Finish navigation) anchored to a highlighted target element, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the card sits on the given side of the target, with a small arrow connecting it back to the target. Top's arrow points down at the target below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the target above it, Left's arrow points right at the target beside it, Right's arrow points left at the target beside it.

Step-position states (3): First step (step counter "1 of 3", only a Next button); Middle step (step counter "2 of 3", both Back and Next buttons); Last step (step counter "3 of 3", a Back button plus a Finish button instead of Next).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, similar in floating-panel language to this system's Tooltip and Popover components, but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The target is a decorative highlighted chip (not a real interactive control), sitting on the ordinary page background outside the card so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 2px solid var(--red-500), box-shadow "0 0 0 3px var(--red-tint)" - so it reads clearly as the highlighted element the tour is pointing at. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the card's own inverted background color. Primary actions (Next/Finish) use background var(--red-500); the Back button is a ghost/outline style using the card's own inverted text color for its border and label (var(--text-hi)/var(--line-strong) would go near-invisible against the inverted background).

Component properties: Target label (string, the highlighted element's text) - currently "New feature". Title (string, bold text at the top of the card body) - currently "AuditField42". Description (string, supporting text below the title) - currently "Get a quick overview of your team's activity in one place.".

tests.from: Get a quick overview of your team's activity in one place.
tests.prompt:
Create a complete Tour component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, step-position state, target label, title, description) - a step-by-step walkthrough card (title + description + step counter + Back/Next or Back/Finish navigation) anchored to a highlighted target element, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the card sits on the given side of the target, with a small arrow connecting it back to the target. Top's arrow points down at the target below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the target above it, Left's arrow points right at the target beside it, Right's arrow points left at the target beside it.

Step-position states (3): First step (step counter "1 of 3", only a Next button); Middle step (step counter "2 of 3", both Back and Next buttons); Last step (step counter "3 of 3", a Back button plus a Finish button instead of Next).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, similar in floating-panel language to this system's Tooltip and Popover components, but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The target is a decorative highlighted chip (not a real interactive control), sitting on the ordinary page background outside the card so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 2px solid var(--red-500), box-shadow "0 0 0 3px var(--red-tint)" - so it reads clearly as the highlighted element the tour is pointing at. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the card's own inverted background color. Primary actions (Next/Finish) use background var(--red-500); the Back button is a ghost/outline style using the card's own inverted text color for its border and label (var(--text-hi)/var(--line-strong) would go near-invisible against the inverted background).

Component properties: Target label (string, the highlighted element's text) - currently "New feature". Title (string, bold text at the top of the card body) - currently "Try the new dashboard". Description (string, supporting text below the title) - currently "AuditField42".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

title: Tour STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Tour component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, step-position state, target label, title, description) - a step-by-step walkthrough card (title + description + step counter + Back/Next or Back/Finish navigation) anchored to a highlighted target element, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the card sits on the given side of the target, with a small arrow connecting it back to the target. Top's arrow points down at the target below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the target above it, Left's arrow points right at the target beside it, Right's arrow points left at the target beside it.

Step-position states (3): First step (step counter "1 of 3", only a Next button); Middle step (step counter "2 of 3", both Back and Next buttons); Last step (step counter "3 of 3", a Back button plus a Finish button instead of Next).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, similar in floating-panel language to this system's Tooltip and Popover components, but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The target is a decorative highlighted chip (not a real interactive control), sitting on the ordinary page background outside the card so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 2px solid var(--red-500), box-shadow "0 0 0 3px var(--red-tint)" - so it reads clearly as the highlighted element the tour is pointing at. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the card's own inverted background color. Primary actions (Next/Finish) use background var(--red-500); the Back button is a ghost/outline style using the card's own inverted text color for its border and label (var(--text-hi)/var(--line-strong) would go near-invisible against the inverted background).

Component properties: Target label (string, the highlighted element's text) - currently "New feature". Title (string, bold text at the top of the card body) - currently "Try the new dashboard". Description (string, supporting text below the title) - currently "Get a quick overview of your team's activity in one place.".

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

OVERVIEW

Tour guides a new user through a sequence of features one at a time - a small card anchored next to a highlighted UI element, with Back/Next navigation and a step counter, used to walk someone through unfamiliar functionality rather than leaving them to discover it alone.

WHEN TO USE

First-time onboarding through key features - a guided walkthrough for new users.
A feature-announcement walkthrough - introducing something new to existing users.
A multi-step setup guide or contextual help sequence - anchored to the actual UI elements involved.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A single, standalone hint about one control - use Tooltip instead of a full multi-step tour.
Reference material a user might want to revisit anytime - use static Documentation or a help panel rather than a one-time guided sequence.
Frequent or repeated interruptions for returning users - a Tour should typically run once (or be easily dismissed permanently), not repeatedly block the same user.

BEST PRACTICES

Keep the sequence short - a handful of steps at most, focused on genuinely non-obvious functionality.
Always let the user skip or exit the tour at any step, not just at the end.
Anchor each step precisely to the real UI element it describes, so the highlighted target and the explanation clearly match.

DO AND DON'T

DO

Step 2 of 3

Filters live here

Narrow long lists without leaving the page.

A short sequence with the position shown, so the user knows how much is left before they commit.

DON'T

Step 9 of 14

This is the Save button

Click Save to save.

Fourteen steps explaining self-evident controls gets dismissed, taking the genuinely useful steps with it.

ACCESSIBILITY

Each step's card is exposed as role="dialog" (like Modal, but non-blocking of the rest of the page: aria-modal="false") with an accessible name and description via aria-labelledby/aria-describedby.
Focus moves into each step's card as it appears - the same per-step focus management Modal uses on open - so keyboard and screen-reader users follow the same sequence as everyone else, then moves on again as the step advances.
Each step is reachable and dismissible by keyboard (Back/Next/Escape), not only by mouse click, and a Skip/Exit control is always keyboard-reachable, not just a small close icon meant for a mouse.
The step count and current position ("Step 2 of 4") are exposed as text content read with the step, not conveyed only by a visual progress dot - and no separate aria-live region is used, since each step's arrival is already announced by focus moving to its dialog.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Tooltip, Popover, Steps.

dark.prompt:
Create a complete Tour component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (placement, step-position state, target label, title, description) - a step-by-step walkthrough card (title + description + step counter + Back/Next or Back/Finish navigation) anchored to a highlighted target element, not a one-off floating div built from scratch each time.

Placements (4): Top, Bottom, Left, Right - the card sits on the given side of the target, with a small arrow connecting it back to the target. Top's arrow points down at the target below it, Bottom's arrow points up at the target above it, Left's arrow points right at the target beside it, Right's arrow points left at the target beside it.

Step-position states (3): First step (step counter "1 of 3", only a Next button); Middle step (step counter "2 of 3", both Back and Next buttons); Last step (step counter "3 of 3", a Back button plus a Finish button instead of Next).

Visual treatment: reads as a proper elevated panel, similar in floating-panel language to this system's Tooltip and Popover components, but inverted against the page like a real overlay should be - near-black background in light theme, near-white in dark theme (background var(--overlay-invert-bg), NOT the normal-surface var(--graphite-900), since that's user-customizable via Foundations and would silently break the inversion), no border (box-shadow "0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)" alone gives it separation from the page), border-radius var(--radius-md). The target is a decorative highlighted chip (not a real interactive control), sitting on the ordinary page background outside the card so it keeps this system's normal, non-inverted styling - background var(--graphite-800), border 2px solid var(--red-500), box-shadow "0 0 0 3px var(--red-tint)" - so it reads clearly as the highlighted element the tour is pointing at. The arrow is a small rotated square (transform:rotate(45deg)) matching the card's own inverted background color. Primary actions (Next/Finish) use background var(--red-500); the Back button is a ghost/outline style using the card's own inverted text color for its border and label (var(--text-hi)/var(--line-strong) would go near-invisible against the inverted background).

Component properties: Target label (string, the highlighted element's text) - currently "New feature". Title (string, bold text at the top of the card body) - currently "Try the new dashboard". Description (string, supporting text below the title) - currently "Get a quick overview of your team's activity in one place.".

<!-- ads:contract -->
## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

{"content":0,"sticky":20,"popover":40,"scrim":60,"dialog":70,"toast":80,"tooltip":90,"rules":"Each overlay gets an explicit owner and close/focus-return path. Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

tests.prompt:
Create a complete Transfer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dual-list widget controlled by properties (type, state, size, left title, right title) - two side-by-side list panels, an available-items "Source" list on the left and a chosen-items "Target" list on the right, each item with its own checkbox, with center-aligned ">" / "<" arrow buttons between the panels to move checked items from one side to the other. This is a standalone panel widget, not a text-field trigger.

Types (2):
- Default: Two plain list panels - available items on the left, chosen items on the right - no search box.
- With search: Same two-panel layout, but each panel gets its own search input above its list, so a long source or target list can be filtered before moving items.

States (4):
- Rest: default appearance.
- Hover: the first source item shows a hover background.
- Focused: the right (">") transfer button shows a visible focus ring.
- Disabled: the whole widget at reduced opacity (40%), checkboxes and arrow buttons non-interactive.

Size: Small - controls each panel's list height (140px). Other options: Small (140px) / Default (180px) / Large (220px).

Component properties: Size (dropdown - Small/Default/Large, controls each panel's list height); Left title (text, e.g. "Source"); Right title (text, e.g. "Target").

- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

- version: 1

Create a complete Transfer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dual-list widget controlled by properties (type, state, size, left title, right title) - two side-by-side list panels, an available-items "Source" list on the left and a chosen-items "Target" list on the right, each item with its own checkbox, with center-aligned ">" / "<" arrow buttons between the panels to move checked items from one side to the other. This is a standalone panel widget, not a text-field trigger.

Types (2):
- Default: Two plain list panels - available items on the left, chosen items on the right - no search box.
- With search: Same two-panel layout, but each panel gets its own search input above its list, so a long source or target list can be filtered before moving items.

States (4):
- Rest: default appearance.
- Hover: the first source item shows a hover background.
- Focused: the right (">") transfer button shows a visible focus ring.
- Disabled: the whole widget at reduced opacity (40%), checkboxes and arrow buttons non-interactive.

Size: Large - controls each panel's list height (220px). Other options: Small (140px) / Default (180px) / Large (220px).

Component properties: Size (dropdown - Small/Default/Large, controls each panel's list height); Left title (text, e.g. "Source"); Right title (text, e.g. "Target").

- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. - deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. - future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.

title: Transfer STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Transfer component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dual-list widget controlled by properties (type, state, size, left title, right title) - two side-by-side list panels, an available-items "Source" list on the left and a chosen-items "Target" list on the right, each item with its own checkbox, with center-aligned ">" / "<" arrow buttons between the panels to move checked items from one side to the other. This is a standalone panel widget, not a text-field trigger.

Types (2):
- Default: Two plain list panels - available items on the left, chosen items on the right - no search box.
- With search: Same two-panel layout, but each panel gets its own search input above its list, so a long source or target list can be filtered before moving items.

States (4):
- Rest: default appearance.
- Hover: the first source item shows a hover background.
- Focused: the right (">") transfer button shows a visible focus ring.
- Disabled: the whole widget at reduced opacity (40%), checkboxes and arrow buttons non-interactive.

Size: Default - controls each panel's list height (180px). Other options: Small (140px) / Default (180px) / Large (220px).

Component properties: Size (dropdown - Small/Default/Large, controls each panel's list height); Left title (text, e.g. "Source"); Right title (text, e.g. "Target").
